title: e2e_node: podresources: skip cpuAlloc check in BeforeEach, not JustBeforeEach
author: rpb-ant
body:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138074 is seeing reliable e2e test failures. I think this is a ginkgo subtlety.

Ginkgo seemingly only runs `AfterEach` hooks at-or-shallower than the node where `Skip()` fired, so the inner `AfterEach` that would restore the kubelet config is never invoked. The leaked feature gate then propagates to every subsequent serial test, which breaks `device_plugin_test.go`

Moving the check to BeforeEach makes it fire before the inner `BeforeEach` runs, so the config is never written. This matches the identical check at `podresources_test.go` (line 1120).

I ran the gate-setting podresources spec on two e2-standard-2 GCE instances in parallel (master and this pr). `master`'s final kubelet had `KubeletPodResourcesListUseActivePods=false` leaked into its config (seen in logs) while the this PR had zero hits and skipped in `BeforeEach` before any kubelet reconfig happened.

title: Introduce Deferred Gen concept to Validation-gen framework
author: lalitc375
body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind api-change
/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This PR re-architects the `validation-gen` framework to support complex validation rules by introducing **Deferred Validation**  concept.
The primary motivation is to solve a "leakage" issue where stateful validation tags (like `+k8s:update=NoModify`) were being applied globally and unconditionally, even when nested inside conditional wrappers like `+k8s:ifEnabled`. Previously, these stateful tags would write to global memory during phase 1 of generation, causing the generator to emit a root-level check that bypassed the user's intended conditional logic.

The new **Deferred Validation** model allows parent wrappers to intercept validation logic via a callback mechanism, ensuring that code is only generated within the appropriate execution context (e.g., inside the `validate.IfOption` closure).

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Fixes: [jpbetz/validation-gen#244](https://github.com/jpbetz/validation-gen/issues/244)

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
This PR includes:
*   Implementation of the `DeferredGen` base framework in the code-generator.
*   Migration of major validators (including `update`, `union`, `subfield`, `list`, and `ifEnabled`) to the deferred model.
*   An update to `validate.IfOption` to support non-pointer types, which was necessary for certain validation scenarios.
*   Updated validation output tests to reflect the new architecture.

Co-authored-by: @thockin

```release-note
NONE
```

title: test/e2e_node_windows: Add Windows node-level e2e tests
author: zylxjtu
body:
## What this PR does

This PR introduces a dedicated `test/e2e_node_windows/` directory for Windows node-level e2e tests, separating them from the existing Linux-focused `test/e2e_node/` package.

## Motivation

kubernetes/kubernetes#129938 proposed adding Windows node-level e2e support, and the effort has been ongoing for some time. We deeply appreciate the thoughtful feedback from sig-node reviewers, and understand there are open concerns about mixing Windows-specific test infrastructure into the existing `test/e2e_node/` package, which has been carefully designed around Linux/systemd assumptions, although we have tried our best to decouple the windows from linux ones

This PR takes a different approach to address those concerns: rather than extending `test/e2e_node/` to accommodate Windows, it places all Windows node-level test code in a completely separate `test/e2e_node_windows/` package. This gives Windows tests full isolation from the Linux test path, while keeping the existing `test/e2e_node/` package untouched.

## What changes

- **New `test/e2e_node_windows/` package** — a self-contained Windows node e2e test suite with its own services layer (`services/kubelet.go`, `services/server.go`, etc.), all gated with `//go:build windows`
- **`test/e2e_node/services/kubelet.go` and `server.go`** — `//go:build linux` tags added to make the Linux/systemd-specific service code explicit, enabling clean coexistence with the new Windows counterparts
- **`test/e2e_node/builder/build.go`** — `//go:build linux` tag added for the same reason
- **`hack/lib/golang.sh`** — the Windows test binary (`e2e_node_windows.test`) is included in the build when `KUBE_BUILD_PLATFORMS` targets Windows, mirroring the existing Linux pattern
- **`test/e2e/feature/feature.go`** — added ownership comment for the `Windows` feature label

## Isolation guarantees

- The new `test/e2e_node_windows/` package is fully gated by `//go:build windows` — it is never compiled on Linux and cannot affect the existing Linux e2e node tests
- The existing `test/e2e_node/` package and its test suite are unchanged in behavior
- The `golang.sh` change is purely additive and does not modify the Linux build path

/sig-node

title: devicemanager: constrain topology hints to device NUMA nodes
author: fanzhangio
body:
## What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

## What this PR does / why we need it

On systems with many NUMA nodes (e.g. NVIDIA GB200 compute trays with 36 OS-visible NUMA nodes, only 2 CPU NUMA nodes), the device manager's `generateDeviceTopologyHints` calls `bitmask.IterateBitMasks` over **all** kubelet-known NUMA nodes. Since `IterateBitMasks` enumerates every non-empty subset, the cost is O(2^n) — with n=34 that is ~17 billion iterations. This causes kubelet to stall indefinitely during topology hint computation and the pod never reaches `Allocate`.

### Root cause
The iteration space is derived from `m.numaNodes`, which includes every NUMA node the OS exposes. On GB200 the majority of those nodes carry only GPU HBM (Coherent Device Memory) and host zero devices for any given
device-plugin resource. Including them inflates n without contributing useful hints.

This PR constrains the bitmask iteration to only the NUMA nodes that actually host available or reusable devices for the requested resource, reducing the search space from 2^n (machine-wide) to 2^k (device-relevant), where k is typically 1–2 on GB200 systems.

### Fix

- Introduce `deviceNUMANodes(resource)`, which collects the NUMA node IDs from **all registered devices** (`m.allDevices[resource]`) regardless of allocation state. `generateDeviceTopologyHints` now iterates only over
those nodes, reducing the search space from 2^n (machine-wide) to 2^k (device-relevant), where k is typically 1–2 on GB200 systems.

- Using `allDevices` (rather than `available ∪ reusable`) ensures that `minAffinitySize` and `Preferred` flags are computed identically to the original code — device-less NUMA nodes contribute zero to `devicesInMask`
and can never reduce `minAffinitySize`, so any mask containing them is always non-preferred. Removing them from iteration is therefore **behavior-preserving** for all existing configurations.

### Changes

1. **`deviceNUMANodes(resource)`** — new helper that returns the sorted list of NUMA node IDs hosting at least one device for the given resource. Falls back to `m.numaNodes` when no topology info exists.

2. **`generateDeviceTopologyHints()`** — now calls `IterateBitMasks(deviceNUMANodes, …)` instead of `IterateBitMasks(m.numaNodes, …)`. No synthetic fallback hint is needed because the iteration already covers every NUMA node that could satisfy a request.

3. **Unit tests** :     
   - `TestDeviceNUMANodes`: validates NUMA node collection from `allDevices` and fallback behavior.
   - `TestGenerateDeviceTopologyHintsFiltersNUMANodes`: verifies that device-less NUMA nodes are excluded from hints, including a 34-device-less-node scenario.
   - `TestFilteredDeviceHintsMergeWithOtherProviders`: confirms that filtered device hints merge correctly with CPU/memory providers through the TopologyManager.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/135541

## How has this been tested?

- All exis

title: hpa: eliminate reconciliation delay on HPA creation and spec changes
author: fedosin
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When an HPA is created or its spec is updated, the controller delays
reconciliation by the full resync period (default 15s, configurable up to 60s)
because `enqueueHPA` uses `queue.AddRateLimited`. This means users must wait
the entire resync interval before their HPA takes effect.

This PR fixes the delay by:

1. Switching `enqueueHPA` from `queue.AddRateLimited` to `queue.Add` so newly
   created HPAs are processed immediately.
2. Adding a `Generation` comparison in `updateHPA` (gated behind the
   `HPAGeneration` feature from #138228) to distinguish spec changes from
   status-only updates: spec changes trigger immediate reconciliation, while
   status-only changes remain rate-limited. When `HPAGeneration` is disabled,
   all updates fall back to rate-limited enqueue (the original behavior).

This preserves the hot-loop prevention from #42715 where the controller's own
status writes would otherwise re-trigger continuous reconciliation. The periodic
resync cadence is also unaffected because `processNextWorkItem` continues to
call `AddRateLimited` after every reconciliation cycle.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Related to #42715
Depends on #138228

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The `Generation` field is bumped by the API server only on spec mutations (when
`HPAGeneration` feature gate is enabled). This makes it a reliable
discriminator: status writes by the controller itself do not bump `Generation`,
so they remain rate-limited and cannot cause a hot-loop.

When the type assertion in `updateHPA` fails (e.g., `DeletedFinalStateUnknown`),
the code falls back to rate-limited enqueue to prevent any theoretical hot-loop.

Additionally, `enqueueHPA` now registers the HPA selector *before* calling
`queue.Add` to avoid a race where immediate reconciliation could start before
selector bookkeeping exists.

Unit tests are added to `horizontal_test.go` covering:
- `enqueueHPA` uses `queue.Add` (not `AddRateLimited`)
- `enqueueHPA` registers selector before queue add
- `updateHPA` with generation bump → immediate enqueue
- `updateHPA` with same generation → rate-limited enqueue
- `updateHPA` with unrecognized object types → fallback to rate-limited enqueue
- `updateHPA` with `HPAGeneration` disabled → all updates rate-limited

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
HPA controller now reconciles newly created and spec-changed HPAs immediately instead of waiting for the full resync period (default 15s).
```

title: fix: accumulate subpath cleanup actions in makeMounts to prevent handle leak
author: timmy-wright
body:
## What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

## What this PR does / why we need it
Fixes a file handle leak in `makeMounts()` that causes emptyDir volumes to fail cleanup on Windows, leaving pods stuck in Terminating state after deletion.

In `makeMounts()`, a single `cleanupAction` variable was overwritten each time `PrepareSafeSubpath()` was called in the volume mount loop. On Windows, `PrepareSafeSubpath` acquires file handles via `syscall.CreateFile` (in `lockAndCheckSubPath` → `lockPath`) to prevent symlink race attacks. Because only the last mount's cleanup function was returned to the caller (`kuberuntime_container.go:255: defer cleanupAction()`), all prior handles leaked permanently. This prevented `os.RemoveAll` from deleting the emptyDir volume directory during pod teardown.

Linux is unaffected because its `PrepareSafeSubpath` uses bind mounts and always returns `cleanupAction = nil`.

## How does this fix it?
Replaces the single `cleanupAction` variable with a `[]func{}` slice accumulator. Each call to `PrepareSafeSubpath` appends its cleanup to the slice, and the composite `cleanupAction` closure invokes all of them when called.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/112630

## Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Fixed a bug where pods with multiple subPath volume mounts on Windows would get stuck in Terminating state because file handles from subPath preparation were leaked, preventing volume cleanup.
```

## Testing
- **Unit test**: `TestMakemountsSubpathCleanupAccumulation` with 5 table-driven cases covering multi-mount cleanup accumulation, single mount, no subpaths, and error paths (verifying earlier cleanups still fire when a later mount fails)
- **E2e test**: Windows-specific test that creates a pod with 3 subPath mounts from a ConfigMap and verifies it terminates cleanly after deletion

/sig node
/sig windows
/area kubelet

closes.title: EmptyDir not being cleaned up after pod terminated with open file handles

title: Fix goroutine leak in storageversionmigrator migrationrunner test
author: myounghasong
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #137970 for issue #134565.

`TestCustomResourceController_Sync` in `pkg/controller/storageversionmigrator/migrationrunner_test.go` calls `NewCustomResourceController`, which creates a workqueue (via `workqueue.NewTypedRateLimitingQueueWithConfig`). The test never shuts it down, leaking the workqueue's `waitingLoop` goroutines.

This PR:
- Replaces `context.Background()` with `context.WithCancel()` and defers `cancel()`
- Adds `defer controller.queue.ShutDown()` to clean up the workqueue

Verified locally with a temporary `goleak.VerifyTestMain`. The other two test files in the same package (`storageversionmigrator_test.go` and `resourceversion_test.go`) construct controller structs directly without a queue, so they do not leak goroutines and are not modified.

/sig api-machinery
/kind bug

- [x] `go test ./pkg/controller/storageversionmigrator/ -count=1` passes

title: KEP-5304, fix: merge same request metadata across drivers
author: oshoval
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Fixes consumer-side metadata merge behavior in `devicemetadata.readRequestDir`.

When a single claim request is allocated across multiple drivers,
each driver writes its own `*-metadata.json` file. Before this
change, merging these files appended `Requests` entries directly, which could
produce duplicate request objects with the same `request.Name`.

This change merges by request name:

- if a request name is new, append it
- if it already exists, append only devices into the existing request entry

This guarantees one merged request entry per request name in the combined result.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/138352
KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5304

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- Scope is intentionally minimal and focused on merge behavior for duplicate
  request names across multiple driver files.

The ResourceClaimController's syncPod method only includes new resource claims in the server-side apply, not existing claims. Since this controller is the owning fieldManager, SSA removes the missing existing keys. This results in flapping between claims when more than one claim is assigned to the Pod.

This fix includes the existing claims in the SSA request.

Fixes #138407 

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
An alternative would be to change `handleClaims` to not just return when it finds an existing claim, but instead add it to the list of claims. This would require changing the signature and meaning of the `newPodClaims`.

Google Gemini was used in preparing this PR.

title: kubelet: enforce ephemeral-storage limits on restartable init containers
author: shachartal
body:
## What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

## What this PR does / why we need it

`containerEphemeralStorageLimitEviction()` only iterates `pod.Spec.Containers` when building the per-container ephemeral-storage threshold map. Restartable init containers (sidecars) are never added to `thresholdsMap`, so a sidecar can exceed its `limits.ephemeral-storage` indefinitely without triggering pod eviction.

This PR adds iteration over `pod.Spec.InitContainers` for restartable init containers when building the threshold map, so the existing per-container comparison covers them.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Fixes #138371

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
-->
```release-note
Fixed a bug where the kubelet did not enforce per-container ephemeral-storage limits on restartable init containers (sidecar containers), allowing them to exceed their declared limit without triggering pod eviction.
```

title: test/e2e/node: make GPU sanity test work on arm64 (sbsa)
author: dims
body:
The [Feature:GPUDevicePlugin] Sanity test embeds
`apt-get install -y cuda-demo-suite-12-5` under `set -e`. NVIDIA's CUDA apt repo publishes cuda-demo-suite-* for x86_64 but NOT for sbsa (confirmed against the public Packages index on
developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2204/{sbsa,x86_64}/). On arm64 the install fails, the container exits 1, pod.Status.Phase becomes Failed, and the subsequent `gomega.Expect(... .Equal(Succeeded))` assertion trips.

Split the demo phase on architecture. On x86_64 keep the existing apt path unchanged. On anything else, build deviceQuery / vectorAdd / bandwidthTest from the public NVIDIA/cuda-samples repo instead. busGrind is exclusive to cuda-demo-suite (no source equivalent in cuda-samples) and is skipped on non-x86_64.

The pattern is the one already in production use by sigs.k8s.io/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu in tests/bats/specs/gpu-cuda-demo-suite.yaml, which has been green on Lambda gpu_1x_gh200.

author: bart0sh
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Small one-line fix:
`GetPlugin` returns (nil, error) on failure. The error check in `unprepareResources` was comparing the plugin pointer to nil instead of checking the error, which is inconsistent with the identical call in `prepareResources` and could mask the actual error in future refactors.

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`DecodeMetadataFromStream` previously skipped any object-level decode or conversion failure while looking for a compatible metadata version. That meant malformed metadata for a supported API version could be silently ignored if a later entry decoded successfully. With this PR:

- Entries whose `apiVersion` is not registered in the local scheme are still skipped silently for forward compatibility.
- Decode failures for registered versions are returned with error immediately.
- Malformed entries, including entries with missing `kind` or missing `apiVersion`, are returned with error immediately.

title: DRA: harmonize ResourceClaim creation metric
author: pohly
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Both kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler create ResourceClaims. Using the same metric (sub-system: "dynamic_resource_allocation", name: "resourceclaim_creates_total") in both components simplifies aggregation across the entire cluster.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/135075

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler now both expose "dynamic_resource_allocation_resourceclaim_creates_total" as metric for number of ResourceClaims created, replacing differently names metrics in each component. The kube-controller-manager metric "resource_claims" gets moved to the same "dynamic_resource_allocation" sub-system.
```

/cc @yliaog @bart0sh 
/assign @dgrisonnet

closes.title: DRA extended resource: decide about metrics name

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
`TestReplicaCalcScaleUpCMExternal` and `TestReplicaCalcScaleUpCMExternalNoLabels` are functionally identical. Both use `metricType: podMetric` with the same inputs and expected outputs. title: pkg/apis/core: allow uint32 Linux UIDs in container status
author: kunalbehbud
body:
## What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig node

## What this PR does / why we need it

Linux UIDs are unsigned 32-bit values, but pod status validation currently uses the existing Kubernetes pod spec UID validator, which is limited to `math.MaxInt32`. When a runtime reports `containerStatus.user.linux.uid` above `2147483647`, kubelet status updates can be rejected even though the reported UID is valid on Linux.

This PR keeps pod spec `runAsUser` and kubelet image user validation on the existing int32 UID range, and only accepts the full unsigned 32-bit Linux UID range for reported container user fields in pod status. GID and supplemental group validation remain unchanged.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Fixes #138525

## Special notes for your reviewer

Added regression coverage for:
- regular, init, and ephemeral container status user UIDs at `math.MaxUint32`
- pod status user UIDs above `math.MaxUint32` being rejected
- existing pod spec `runAsUser` validation remaining unchanged

## Test evidence

```console
go test ./pkg/apis/core/validation -run 'TestValidatePodSpec|TestValidatePodUpdate|TestValidatePodStatusUpdate' -count=1
GOOS=linux GOARCH=386 go test ./pkg/apis/core/validation -run 'TestValidatePodSpec|TestValidatePodUpdate|TestValidatePodStatusUpdate' -count=1
go test k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/validation -run TestIsValidUserID -count=1
go test ./pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime -run TestVerifyRunAsNonRoot -count=1
hack/verify-typecheck.sh
make test WHAT="./staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/validation ./pkg/apis/core/validation ./pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime" KUBE_RACE=-race
```

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed pod status validation for reported Linux container user UIDs so values above 2147483647 and up to the unsigned 32-bit UID limit are accepted.
```

#### AI Disclosure

AI tooling was used to assist in preparing this PR. All changes and tests were reviewed and run locally by the author.

closes.title: "containerStatus.user.linux.uid rejects valid Linux UIDs > INT32_MAX"

title: bump cos-gpu-installer to v2.5.8 for COS M125

body:
#### What type of PR is this?

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-device-plugin-gpu` and `ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-device-plugin-gpu-1-36` have been failing since ~2026-04-28 00:00 UTC with:

```
Timed out after 600.000s.
nvidia GPUs not available on Node: "kt2-a3452892-ed42-minion-group-4w11"
```

The GCE node image family in `cluster/gce/config-default.sh` was updated to `cos-125-lts` but `test/e2e/testing-manifests/gpu/gce/nvidia-driver-installer.yaml` was never updated to match. `cos-gpu-installer:v2.5.7` is only suitable for COS M121 — on `cos-125-19216-220-150` nodes it crashes immediately into `CrashLoopBackOff`, so the NVIDIA driver is never installed, `nvidia.com/gpu` never appears in node capacity, and all GPU tests time out. Both green and red builds ran the identical Kubernetes commit SHA, confirming this is a pure infrastructure failure.

Bumps the installer image to `v2.5.8`, the first version listed in the [COS M125 release notes](https://cloud.google.com/container-optimized-os/docs/release-notes/m125). Same fix pattern as PR #134495 (M109→M121) and test-infra PR #35661.

title: Fix nil pointer dereference in Windows memory eviction threshold notifier
author: rzlink
body:
## What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

## What this PR does / why we need it

Fixes a nil pointer dereference bug in the Windows memory eviction threshold notifier.

In `checkMemoryUsage()` (`memory_threshold_notifier_windows.go`), when `GetPerformanceInfo()` fails, the error is logged but execution continues. The next line dereferences `perfInfo` (which is nil), causing a panic:

```go
perfInfo, err := winstats.GetPerformanceInfo()
if err != nil {
    logger.Error(err, "...")
    // missing return - falls through to nil dereference below
}
commitLimitBytes := perfInfo.CommitLimitPages * perfInfo.PageSize  // PANIC
```

### Fix

1. **Add early return** after the error log to prevent the nil dereference.
2. **Fix typo** in variable name: `commmiLimitBytes` → `commitLimitBytes` (triple 'm').

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

None

## Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fix nil pointer dereference in Windows memory eviction threshold notifier when GetPerformanceInfo() fails.
```

title: Replace openssl speed CPU burner in summary_test.go
author: saschagrunert
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The `openssl speed -multi $(nproc)` command added in #138423 causes the `ContainerMetrics` cadvisor test to fail on CRI-O conformance (ci-node-crio-conformance) by exceeding upper bounds for `container_fs_writes_total`, `container_blkio_device_usage_total` and `container_memory_failures_total`.

title: optimize CEL admission policies
author: lalitc375
body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This PR optimizes the CEL admission policy evaluation pipeline to significantly reduce CPU usage and garbage collection pressure.

Previously, the CEL admission environment prepared variables like `object` and `oldObject` by passing them through `convertObjectToUnstructured`. This relied heavily on generic JSON reflection loops and allocations, making it very expensive for high-throughput admission controllers.

This PR introduces `UnstructuredReflectToVal`, a zero-allocation reflection-based utility that lazily traverses structured Go objects to construct CEL `ref.Val` representations. This mimics standard unstructured conversion while bypassing expensive full-map allocation and serializer lookups.

Key Changes:
1. **Lazy Conversion Pipeline**: Integrates `UnstructuredReflectToVal` into the `VersionedAttributes` lazy conversion pipeline (`LazyObject.CELValue`) to optimize admission variable preparation.
2. **Robust Nil-Handling**: Implements robust pointer, interface, map, and slice nil-handling to map Go nil values to JSON-equivalent `NullValue` objects. 
3. **Custom Marshaling**: Adds custom marshaling resolution for both pointer and value receiver implementations (`json.Marshaler` / `ToUnstructured`), including dynamically wrapper-addressing struct value fields.
4. **Structural Field Alignment**: Aligns structural field selection in `lookupField` to correctly return `NullValue` (instead of omitting) for non-omitempty nil fields.
5. **Equivalence Testing**: Introduces a comprehensive equivalence test suite (`converter_equivalence_test.go`) verifying absolute behavioral alignment with the Kubernetes `runtime.DefaultUnstructuredConverter.ToUnstructured` serialization.



#### Benchmark Results:
I've run benchmarks comparing the old and new setup. You can view the full benchmark files and results in this [GitHub Gist](https://gist.github.com/lalitc375/d895a5ebfc7292bb42f560b55d677ee6).

**Highlights:**
- `BenchmarkRealisticPod_Setup`: **~96% reduction in ns/op** (53320 ns -> 2098 ns) and significant drop in allocations (216 -> 2 allocs/op).
- `BenchmarkRealisticNestedField_MutliplePolicies (accessing same field in the all policies)`: **~86% reduction in ns/op** (379.6 ns -> 50.07 ns) and zero allocations.
- `BenchmarkVAPSEvaluation_9Policies ( random fields in all policies)`: Performance improved from 89006 ns/op to 58160 ns/op with a 63% reduction in allocs (527 -> 191).

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Part of #131520

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
Integration tests under `test/integration/apiserver/cel/...` have been verified to pass locally. The new `converter_equivalence_test.go` suite guarantees behavioral parity with the existing standard unstructured conversion across nested/inlined structs, omitempty tags, and custom marshaler implementations.

title: apiserver: pass context with ReqInfo to AllowUnconditionalUpdate and AllowCreateOnUpdate
author: pohly
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This enables implementing different behavior for AllowUnconditionalUpdate and AllowCreateOnUpdate depending on the API version, which can be found in ReqInfo.APIVersion. The specific need for this is to switch from AllowUnconditionalUpdate=true (not recommended!) to false in v1 of resource.k8s.io DeviceTaintRule.

This is done by adding the missing context parameter to the existing methods instead of adding a new optional interface because a) the resulting implementation is simpler and gets checked by the compiler and b) the Go API guarantees of k8s.io/apiserver are more relaxed than in other modules because it's less used downstream.

Example implementation:

    func (*deviceTaintRuleStrategy) AllowUnconditionalUpdate(ctx context.Context) bool {
           reqInfo, _ := request.RequestInfoFrom(ctx)
           if reqInfo != nil && reqInfo.APIVersion == "v1" {
                   // Should have done that already earlier. Better late than never...
                   return false
           }
           // Historic behavior for v1beta2 and older, cannot change that anymore.
           return true
    }


#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Required for https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138676.

title: Fix ContainerMetrics cadvisor test flake for block I/O metrics
author: saschagrunert
body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind flake

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
The test pod's `echo` writes (~11 bytes) stay in page cache and never reach the block device within the 60-second test window. This leaves the cgroup `io.stat` empty, so cadvisor does not emit `container_blkio_device_usage_total`, `container_fs_reads_bytes_total`, or `container_fs_writes_bytes_total`.
This PR replaces the `echo` with `dd conv=fsync` to force data through the block layer. Once `io.stat` has a device entry, all fields are present (even zeros), so all metrics pass.

Also increases the `UsageCoreNanoSeconds` upper bound from `1e11` to `1e12` for the container and pod-level CPU checks. The cumulative CPU time can exceed 100s on slower architectures like ppc64le where the `dd` CPU burner loop accumulates faster than expected.

Fixes #138843
Refers to #138753

title: kubelet/eviction: stop monitoring loop on context cancellation
author: alexmchughdev
body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
The eviction manager's monitoring goroutine in `pkg/kubelet/eviction/eviction_manager.go` ran an unbounded `for {}` with no observation of the parent context:

```go
go func() {
    for {
        evictedPods, err := m.synchronize(ctx, diskInfoProvider, podFunc)
        if evictedPods != nil && err == nil {
            ...
            m.waitForPodsCleanup(logger, podCleanedUpFunc, evictedPods)
        } else {
            if err != nil { logger.Error(err, "...") }
            time.Sleep(monitoringInterval)   // <-- uninterruptible
        }
    }
}()
```

On kubelet shutdown the loop kept executing `synchronize()` / `waitForPodsCleanup()`, and the bare `time.Sleep(monitoringInterval)` between iterations was uninterruptible, so the goroutine outlived the kubelet's context and leaked.

This PR:
- checks `ctx.Err()` at the top of every iteration so the loop returns promptly once the parent context is cancelled, and
- replaces the bare `time.Sleep` with a `select` on `ctx.Done()` so a pending sleep doesn't delay shutdown.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
None

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
The change preserves the existing cadence (sleep only when no eviction occurred and no error path is exercised) and reuses the parent context that `Start` already accepts; no new plumbing is required.

Tests: `go test -count=1 -short ./pkg/kubelet/eviction/...` passes.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
kubelet: the eviction manager's monitoring goroutine now exits promptly when the kubelet's context is cancelled, fixing a goroutine leak on shutdown.
```

title: DRA: fix AllocationModeAll with consumed counters
author: takonomura
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When handling a ResourceClaim request with `allocationMode: All`, the structured DRA allocator precomputes all matching devices. That code path did not store the source pool in the `deviceWithID` candidate.

If one of those devices consumed shared counters, `checkAvailableCounters` dereferenced the missing pool and kube-scheduler panicked while filtering the Pod.

This PR sets the pool for `AllocationModeAll` device candidates in the stable, incubating, and experimental allocator variants, and adds a shared regression test for `AllocationModeAll` with consumed counters.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #138882

The new regression test fails with the original nil pointer panic if the `pool: pool` assignment is removed from the `AllocationModeAll` candidate construction path.

title: scheduler: add PreQueueingHint extension point to narrow pod evaluation on events
author: geetasg
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

   /kind feature
   /sig scheduling

   #### What this PR does / why we need it:

   Adds a `PreQueueingHintFn` extension point to the scheduling framework, called once per event to return a set of pod keys to evaluate instead of scanning all unschedulable pods. This addresses the O(N) requeue bottleneck identified in #138095 using the extension-point approach agreed upon in #138531.

   The DRA plugin implements `PreQueueingHintFn` for ResourceClaim events: for ResourceClaimTemplate-based claims (per-pod claims with a Pod OwnerReference), it returns only the owning pod's key, reducing the requeue path from O(N) to O(1). For shared claims or non-templated claims without a single pod owner, it returns nil to fall back to evaluating all pods
   (existing behavior).

   Additionally, ResourceClaim event handling is decoupled from the informer thread using an async workqueue, preventing the informer from blocking on scheduling queue lock acquisition during claim events.

   Both optimizations are gated behind the `SchedulerPreQueueingHints` feature gate (alpha, default=false).

   #### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

   Fixes #138095
   Supersedes #138531

   #### Special notes for your reviewer:

   This implements the extension-point approach recommended by @pohly, @mm4tt, and @macsko in #138531 — plugin-specific logic stays in the plugin, the framework provides a generic `PreQueueingHintFn` that any plugin can implement.

   AI tools (Kiro CLI) were used to assist with development and testing of this change.


   #### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
No


```release-note
Added a new beta feature gate SchedulerPreQueueingHints (on by default). When enabled, scheduler plugins can provide a PreQueueingHintFn that narrows the set of pods evaluated on cluster events, improving scheduling throughput. The DRA plugin implements this to optimize ResourceClaimTemplate-based workloads.
```

closes.title: DRA: scheduler performance issue with ResourceClaim event handling

title: [DRA] Partitionable Device Performance Optimization
author: troychiu
body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
During scale testing for Partitionable Devices, we observed a severe performance regression where the scheduling throughput was **~3 pods/second** for partitionable devices, comparing to **~100 pods/second** for non-partitionable devices. Profiling identified `GatherPools` as the primary CPU bottleneck.

### The Problem
To support cross-node counter pools, the allocator put all counter slices to `slicesShared` and `GatherPools` marked all counter slices as unconditionally "relevant" to the target scheduling node, regardless of its actual node affinity or node name.

In a multi-node cluster with node-local partitionable device pools, this eager relevance check led to a cascading performance overhead:
1. For every scheduling cycle on target node `A`, `GatherPools` would eagerly pull the counter slices for all other nodes (e.g., node `B`, node `C`).
2. Because the corresponding device slices for node `B` and `C` are node-local and filtered out as irrelevant, the scheduler constructed "partial" pools for node `B` and `C`.
3. Since these foreign pools were incomplete on node `A`, they failed the `isComplete` check.
4. This repeatedly triggered the expensive fallback scan (`checkSlicesInPool`) for **every single irrelevant pool** on **every node**.

### The Fix
This PR removes the `len(slice.Spec.SharedCounters) > 0` check, which puts all counter slices to slicesShared. Counter slices are now filtered using standard relevance rules (matching `NodeName`, `AllNodes`, or `NodeSelector`).

This is safe and preserves complete functionality:
*   **Node-Local Pools**: Both the counter slice and device slice match the target node, allowing `GatherPools` to assemble a complete pool in the first pass.
*   **Cross-Node Shared Pools**: If a shared counter slice is published on a different node, the target node's gathered slices will be incomplete. The existing completeness check will catch this and call the fallback `checkSlicesInPool` to correctly fetch the missing counter slice from the cluster cache.

### Performance Results
Verified with the scale tests
*   Without this PR: ~3 pods/second
*   With this PR: **~100 pods/second**


### Notes
The scale tests are achieve by modifying https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/integration/scheduler_perf/dra.go#L173 to create device slices and counter slices instead and reuse SteadyStateClusterResourceClaimTemplate test suite. I didn’t use https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/integration/scheduler_perf/dra/partitionabledevices/performance-config.yaml because the slices created from this test suite use node selectors.

Ideally, I am thinking if we can run GatherPools only once for scheduling a Pod. For example, we run GatherPools in PreFilter and reuse this information in Filter. However, that's out of the scope of this PR.

cc @mortent @johnbelamaric  @pohly

title: Fix pullmanager lock stripe normalization
author: rajvardhanpatil07
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig node

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`NewStripedLockSet` normalized the allocated lock slice to at most 31 entries, but kept the original requested size in `StripedLockSet.size`. `Lock` and `Unlock` then hashed keys modulo the original requested size, which could index beyond the allocated lock slice when `maxParallelImagePulls` was greater than 31.

This removes the separate stored size and uses the backing lock slice length as the stripe count, so the hash modulus always matches the indexable range.

The PR also adds regression coverage for a large requested stripe count such as `500`, matching the shape of the panic reported in #138935.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #138935

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The focused regression test intentionally chooses a key that would hash outside the allocated 31-lock range when using the original requested size.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed a kubelet panic in image pull credential verification when maxParallelImagePulls is configured above 31.
```

title: test/e2e/common/node: poll for eventually-consistent state to reduce flakiness
author: rzlink
body:
## What type of PR is this?
/kind cleanup
/kind flake

## What this PR does / why we need it

These tests have race conditions where they assume immediate state visibility after a pod transitions to `Running`. The current code works on fast runtimes but is fundamentally racy: kubelet log streaming, log file flushing, and container status updates are eventually consistent, not synchronous.

Switching to `gomega.Eventually` polling makes the tests deterministic. The success path on fast runtimes is unchanged (polling succeeds on first attempt), but the tests now correctly handle scenarios where state takes a moment to propagate. This benefits any environment where containers may take longer to start (VM-isolated runtimes such as Kata, gVisor, and Windows Hyper-V; overloaded CI VMs; shared multi-tenant clusters).

### Changes

- **`ephemeral_containers.go`** (both `should be added` and `should update` tests): the `polo` log-content check is polled via `gomega.Eventually` with `f.Timeouts.PodStartShort`. The container may report Running before its first stdout has been flushed.

- **`lifecycle_hook.go`** (`ignore terminated container`): use `f.Timeouts.PodDelete` instead of `gracePeriod*time.Second` for the termination wait. The actual correctness check (container's intrinsic `StartedAt`/`FinishedAt` < `sleepSeconds`) is unchanged and unaffected by how long we waited.

- **`pods.go`** (`retrieving logs from the container over websockets`): poll the websocket open and read via `gomega.Eventually`. The container can be reported Running before its first stdout line has been flushed, so opening the websocket immediately may return an empty or partial buffer.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes

None — observed as recurring flakes in capz-windows-master-hyperv CI but the underlying races affect any sufficiently slow environment.

## Special notes for your reviewer

These are pure robustness improvements:
- No test semantics change — same things are validated
- No happy-path slowdown — polling succeeds on first attempt when state is already there
- No new dependencies, no new test infrastructure

## Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

title: Fix error formatting and use proper error wrapping in HPA controller
author: fedosin
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR makes two improvements to error handling in the HPA controller:

**1. Fix format-string argument order in object metric error messages**

The error format strings in `GetObjectMetricReplicas` and `GetObjectPerPodMetricReplicas` in the HPA replica calculator had the `fmt.Errorf` arguments in the wrong order relative to the format verbs.

The format string was:
```
"unable to get metric %s: %v on %s %s/%s", metricName, objectRef.Kind, namespace, objectRef.Name, err
```

This caused `objectRef.Kind` to be printed where the error (`%v`) should appear, and `err` to be formatted by the final `%s` meant for `objectRef.Name`. The resulting error messages were misleading and made debugging object metric failures harder.

Fixed by reordering the format string to the idiomatic Go pattern (context first, error last):
```
"unable to get metric %s on %s %s/%s: %w", metricName, objectRef.Kind, namespace, objectRef.Name, err
```

**2. Use `%w` for proper error wrapping across the package**

Replaced `%v` with `%w` for error arguments in all `fmt.Errorf` calls throughout the HPA controller (`horizontal.go`), replica calculator (`replica_calculator.go`), and metrics client (`metrics/client.go`). This enables proper error wrapping so that callers can use `errors.Is` and `errors.As` to inspect underlying errors.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- The first commit fixes the argument ordering bug in `GetObjectMetricReplicas` and `GetObjectPerPodMetricReplicas`.
- The second commit is a broader cleanup that replaces `%v` → `%w` for all error arguments in `fmt.Errorf` across the `pkg/controller/podautoscaler` package (30 occurrences across 3 files).
- Two `%v` usages were intentionally left unchanged: integer format arguments in `computeReplicasForMetrics`, and the sentinel error pattern on line 836 of `horizontal.go` where `%v` is used for `err` alongside a deliberate `%w` for `errSpec`.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed incorrect error message formatting in the HPA controller when object metric retrieval fails. Error messages now correctly display the metric name, object kind, namespace, object name, and the underlying error. Also improved error wrapping across the HPA controller to use %w instead of %v, enabling proper error chain inspection.
```

title: Use direct I/O for ContainerMetrics cadvisor test
author: saschagrunert
body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind flake

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Overlayfs does not support cgroupv2 writeback accounting. Buffered writes (even with `conv=fsync`) get attributed to the root cgroup instead of the container's cgroup. This causes cadvisor to see an empty `io.stat`, making `container_blkio_device_usage_total`, `container_fs_reads_bytes_total`, and `container_fs_writes_bytes_total` permanently absent.

Switches to `oflag=direct` for writes and adds `iflag=direct` reads to bypass the page cache entirely. Direct I/O is always attributed to the issuing process's cgroup regardless of filesystem type.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
#138843

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
This is a follow-up to #138851 which used `conv=fsync` but did not fix the flake because overlayfs writeback accounting attributes I/O to the root cgroup on cgroupv2.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

title: Fix storage tests to support declarative validation enablement
author: jpbetz
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Declarative validation is implemented on versioned types. Storage tests have historically been written against the internal type and the vast majority of the tests are version independent.

In-tree API strategies automatically run declarative validation on every create/update. If we were to set `DeclarativeEnforcement: true`, declarative validation errors are raised and "could not find requestInfo in context" is raised because the declarative validation code path needs the API `GroupVersion` from `RequestInfo` to convert the internal object to the versioned type before calling scheme.Validate.

In production this never happens because `RequestInfo` is always set before the strategy is invoked.

This was the only blocker I found preventing `DeclarativeEnforcement: true` from being set on all in-tree APIs.

title: fix(csi): preserve mount dir when NodePublish fails on a remount
author: aramase
body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When `CSIDriver.spec.requiresRepublish=true`, kubelet periodically calls
`NodePublishVolume` to refresh volume contents. If a republish call
returns a final error, kubelet deletes the host mount directory and
`vol_data.json` in `csi_mounter.SetUpAt`. The pod's bind mount is
already pointing at that directory, so the pod ends up seeing stale or
empty contents and subsequent successful republishes cannot repair it.

The reconciler already knows whether a call is a remount via its
`isRemount` parameter. This PR threads that into `volume.MounterArgs`
and uses it in the CSI mounter to skip the cleanup on remount. The
existing `!mounterArgs.ReconstructedVolume` guard is preserved.

title: Fix kubelet startup failure when restoring legacy V3 CPU manager checkpoints
author: weizhoublue
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
 
#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Trigger scenario
    A node previously ran a version that wrote a V3 CPU manager checkpoint to disk.  That checkpoint’s checksum was computed using the legacy type identity CPUManagerCheckpoint.  The node is then upgraded to the current code, which first tries to read the file as V4, fails, and falls back to V3.   During V3 restore, checksum verification is performed against the new concrete type name CPUManagerCheckpointV3.

this leads to:
  - Kubelet fails to restore CPU manager state during startup.
  - The V3 checkpoint is incorrectly reported as corrupted.
  - Restore then falls through V2 and V1 parsing paths, which also fail.
  - Startup ends with a fatal restore error, and kubelet does not come up unless the checkpoint is removed manually.


  Root cause
In PR #137820,   CPUManagerCheckpointV3 was changed from a type alias to a distinct struct.
 Checksum generation and verification became asymmetric:
      - MarshalCheckpoint() already rewrites CPUManagerCheckpointV3 to CPUManagerCheckpoint before hashing, to preserve compatibility.
      - VerifyChecksum() used only ck.Verify(cp), which hashes the real current type name CPUManagerCheckpointV3.
  - Same logical data, different type name in the hash input, different checksum.

PR #137820,

title: E2E node: enable using release archives for periodic jobs, simplified
author: pohly
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Periodic jobs can be run with less resources in Prow when they merely download the latest pre-built release archives instead of building Kubernetes from source. This PR enables that by:
- Building the functionality of mounter and gcp-credentials-provider into e2e_node.test, activated by invoking that binary through a symlink (i.e., with a different os.Args[0]).
- Stopping to build those separate binaries, using e2e_node.test instead.
- Getting the path to existing binaries from `kubetest2 noop --test=node` when that is told to release archives.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

This is a variant of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139096 which avoids touching existing files. If this experiment doesn't work out, the new files can be removed without breaking `git blame` for the existing files.

The alternative would be to put the additional binaries into the release archives. The approach with extending e2e_node.test is used instead because e2e_node.test is already contained in the released tar balls and making it self-contained avoids putting more knowledge about E2E node testing into the release build process.

Besides avoiding changes to the build rules, bundling the functionality also has a slight size advantage: the size of e2e_node.test increases by 10KB, whereas the other two separate commands would add 10MB.

In earlier revisions this PR completely replaced `kubetest2` by including its own acquisition of a GCP project by calling Boskos. But bootstrapping a Prow job (compiling or downloading e2e_node.test) was still a gap. Now the intended usage is `kubetest2 noop --test=node -- --use-binaries-from-package ...` in a periodic job (similar to the ginkgo aka kops tester) and `kubetest2 noop -test=node -- --build-binaries` in a presubmit (new mode, added for symmetry). In both modes `e2e_node.test remote` is called instead of `make test-e2e-node`.

Depends on https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kubetest2/pull/338.


title: DRA E2E: improve DRAExtendedResource tests go GA graduation
author: bart0sh
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Improves DRAExtendedResource test coverage for GA graduation. The KEP requires the following mixed-node scenarios to be tested:

- Cluster with some nodes using device plugin and others using DRA for the same resource name
- Verify pods can be scheduled to either type of node appropriately
- Ensure one node cannot have both device plugin and DRA for same resource simultaneously
- Validate node transition: remove device plugin, add DRA driver on same node

The first two points are already covered by the existing `must run pods with extended resource on dra nodes and device plugin nodes` test. The transition scenario is covered by the existing `process extended resources after device plugin uninstall` test. 

This PR adds the remaining coverage:

Same-node precedence test `must prefer device plugin over DRA when both advertise the same resource on a node`:
when both a device plugin and a DRA driver advertise the same resource name on one node, filterExtendedResources takes the DRA path only when allocatable == 0, so the device plugin wins and no special ResourceClaim is created. This effectively enforces the "one node cannot have both" invariant: even if both mechanisms are present, only one is active for a given pod, and the result is observable via ExtendedResourceClaimStatus.

DP -> DRA transition: strengthens process extended resources after device plugin uninstall with an ExtendedResourceClaimStatus assertion, explicitly confirming the DRA claim path is taken after device plugin removal — not just that the pod runs.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/138447

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

#### Benchmark results

10,000 HPAs, 100 pods/HPA, 10 namespaces, 96-core machine.

**Throughput (reconciliations/second):**

| Workers | Current (BiMultimap) | Proposed (SelectorStore) | Speedup |
|---------|---------------------|------------------------|---------|
| 50 | 2,635 | 444,671 | 169× |
| 100 | 2,600 | 506,873 | 195× |

Current throughput **degrades** with more workers (increased contention). Proposed throughput **scales** with workers until CPU saturation.

**Contention (100 workers):**

| | Avg lock wait per operation |
|---|---|
| Current | 38.2 ms |
| Proposed | 0.178 ms |
| Reduction | **214×** |

**Memory:**

| | Bytes/HPA (10 namespaces) | Bytes/HPA (100 namespaces) |
|---|---|---|
| Current | 474 | 474 |
| Proposed | 226 | 131 |

**Allocations per operation (100 workers):**

| | Bytes/op | Allocs/op |
|---|---|---|
| Current | 6,148,911 | 71,303 |
| Proposed | 563,203 | 30,100 |

#### Impact

With 100 workers and 15s resync period:

- **Current**: 2,600 ops/s → workers spend 99.7% of time blocked on the mutex. Selector overlap check alone consumes seconds of wall clock per cycle.
- **Proposed**: 500K+ ops/s → selector check becomes negligible.

This changes the cri-api value field from `string` to `bytes`. This encodes identically on the wire, but removes the requirement that the value be valid utf-8. title: Fix Windows file locking race condition in Kubelet tests
author: dom4ha
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind flake

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Fixes a Windows-specific test cleanup race condition in `TestNewMainKubeletStandAlone` and `TestNewMainKubeletWithCertAndCAReloadingEnabled`. 

On Windows nodes, the file system prevents unlinking/deleting files or directories that are still held open by other active processes. During test teardown, `t.Cleanup` calls `os.RemoveAll` on the temp directory immediately after context cancellation. However, the asynchronous garbage collection goroutines can take a moment to fully exit, causing the cleanup to fail with a `The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process` error.

Retrying `os.RemoveAll` with a small backoff (up to 10 retries with 100ms sleeps) to allow background goroutines to release their file/directory handles.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

I encountered this flake on a CI run of `pull-kubernetes-unit-windows-master`.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
NONE
```

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`EventedPLEG` previously acted as an alternative PLEG implementation. When enabled, it wrote pod status to the kubelet cache and emitted `PodLifecycleEvent`s directly, while `GenericPLEG` ran with a much longer relist period and served as a fallback.

That design gave two components responsibility for publishing runtime state and introduced cache ownership, timestamp ordering, and `SyncPod` consistency concerns.

GenericPLEG now supports on-demand per-pod relisting through #137362. - `GenericPLEG` always runs at its normal relist period and remains the sole PLEG implementation.

- The watcher uses selected CRI container termination events as low-latency hints for crash-like transitions that may occur independently of `SyncPod`.

title: batch/job: Fix scheduling directives mutation for not-yet-started suspended Jobs
author: kannon92
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind regression

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When the `MutableSchedulingDirectivesForSuspendedJobs` feature gate is enabled (Beta in 1.36), modifications to scheduling directives on a suspended Job are rejected if the `JobSuspended=True` condition hasn't been set yet by the job controller. This breaks external controllers like MultiKueue that inject scheduling directives immediately after creating a suspended Job.

The fix preserves the `notStarted` path as an OR condition alongside the `JobSuspended` condition check, so that suspended Jobs that have never started can still have their scheduling directives mutated — matching pre-1.36 behavior.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #139281

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The one-line fix is in `pkg/registry/batch/job/strategy.go`. The condition changes from:

```go
suspended && batchvalidation.IsConditionTrue(oldJob.Status.Conditions, batch.JobSuspended) && oldJob.Status.Active == 0
```

to:

```go
suspended && (notStarted || (batchvalidation.IsConditionTrue(oldJob.Status.Conditions, batch.JobSuspended) && oldJob.Status.Active == 0))
```

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed a regression in 1.36 where modifications to scheduling directives (nodeSelector, tolerations, node affinity) on suspended Jobs were rejected if the JobSuspended condition had not yet been set by the job controller.
```

title: noderestriction: prevent kubelet updates to NodeAllocatableResourceClaimStatuses
author: faganihajizada
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The NodeRestriction admission plugin already forbids the kubelet from mutating `pod.status.ResourceClaimStatuses` and `pod.status.ExtendedResourceClaimStatus` via the pod-status subresource, but it does not yet enforce the same boundary for the sibling `pod.status.NodeAllocatableResourceClaimStatuses` field gated by the `DRANodeAllocatableResources` feature gate.

The kubelet status manager already treats the field as not-kubelet-owned and preserves it across status syncs (see commit [9fd706ccd90](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/9fd706ccd90dd4596ef5d92796b6e058dd4f51ad
), "kubelet: do not destroy nodeAllocatableResourceClaimStatuses"). This PR mirrors that boundary in admission so the kubelet cannot stomp on a value the scheduler is responsible for, alongside the existing `ExtendedResourceClaimStatus` check in the same plugin.

`DRANodeAllocatableResources` is alpha and default-off in v1.36, so this is future-proofing rather than a fix for an observed bug.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

Related precedent: #138792.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The new check uses `apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual` inline rather than introducing a third hand-rolled helper next to `resourceClaimStatusesEqual` and `extendedResourceClaimStatusEqual`. `NodeAllocatableResourceClaimStatus.Resources` is a `map[ResourceName]resource.Quantity`, and `Semantic.DeepEqual` already canonicalises `resource.Quantity` via `Cmp`, so the inline form is shorter and more correct than a reflect-based equality function would be.

Skew implication: a pre-`9fd706ccd90` kubelet talking to an apiserver with this check, with `DRANodeAllocatableResources` explicitly enabled, will see its destructive status patches correctly rejected. This is the same risk profile as the existing `ExtendedResourceClaimStatus` check and is the desired behavior.

/sig auth
/sig node

title: DRA: pass ListTypeAttributes to AllocatorFeatures
author: johnahull
body:
## Summary

- Pass `EnableDRAListTypeAttributes` to `AllocatorFeatures()` so the experimental allocator is selected when the `DRAListTypeAttributes` feature gate is enabled

## Problem

KEP-5491 added the `DRAListTypeAttributes` feature gate and implemented list-type attribute intersection matching in the experimental allocator (`allocator_experimental.go`). However, the feature gate was only wired to the CEL cache (`cel.Features`), not to `AllocatorFeatures()`.

Without this fix, the scheduler always selects the incubating allocator (which doesn't support list attributes), even when `DRAListTypeAttributes=true`. The experimental allocator's intersection matching code is never reached.

## Test plan

- Enable `DRAListTypeAttributes` feature gate on API server and scheduler
- Create ResourceSlice devices with `ints` (list) attributes
- Create ResourceClaim with `matchAttribute` referencing a list attribute
- Verify the scheduler selects devices using non-empty intersection matching

Tested on a bare-metal cluster (Dell R7725, AMD EPYC 9825, NPS4) with 4 DRA drivers publishing `numaNode` as a list attribute. Without this fix, all `matchAttribute` claims with list attributes fail to allocate. With this fix, intersection matching works correctly.

title: Fix: pv_collector_total_pv_count reporting N/A plugin for all CSI-provisioned PVs
author: dfajmon
body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug
/kind regression

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The metric `pv_collector_total_pv_count` (which feeds the `kube_persistentvolume_plugin_type_counts` recording rule) reports `plugin_name="N/A"` for all CSI-provisioned PersistentVolumes instead of the correct `kubernetes.io/csi:<driver>` value.

**Root cause:** Commit 9e29f95618c ("Refactor controller-manager volume plugins") replaced `ProbeControllerVolumePlugins` with `ProbeProvisionableRecyclableVolumePlugins` for the PV binder controller. The new function filters plugins to only those implementing `ProvisionableVolumePlugin`, `DeletableVolumePlugin`, or `RecyclableVolumePlugin`. The CSI plugin (`kubernetes.io/csi`) implements none of these interfaces — it delegates all operations to external CSI drivers — so it was silently dropped from `volumePluginMgr`.

`metrics.Register` was still passed `&ctrl.volumePluginMgr`, so at metric collection time `getPVPluginName()` called `pluginMgr.FindPluginBySpec()` for each PV. For any CSI PV, this returned `ErrNoPluginMatched`, causing the code to fall back to the `pluginNameNotAvailable` sentinel (`"N/A"`).

**Fix:** Initialize a dedicated `metricsPluginMgr` from `ProbePersistentVolumePlugins` (which returns all plugins with no filter, including CSI) and pass that to `metrics.Register` instead of `volumePluginMgr`. The operational `volumePluginMgr` (used for provisioning/recycling) is unchanged.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The offending commit is 9e29f95618c. Before that change, the old `ProbeControllerVolumePlugins` included the CSI plugin unconditionally, so `volumePluginMgr` could resolve CSI PVs. The refactor correctly narrowed `volumePluginMgr` for operational purposes but inadvertently broke metric collection, which needs a broader plugin set.

The fix intentionally keeps `volumePluginMgr` narrow (provisionable/deletable/recyclable only) and introduces a separate `metricsPluginMgr` to avoid any unintended side effects on the provisioning/recycling paths.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed `pv_collector_total_pv_count` metric reporting `plugin_name="N/A"` for CSI-provisioned PersistentVolumes. The label now correctly shows `kubernetes.io/csi:<driver-name>` (e.g. `kubernetes.io/csi:ebs.csi.aws.com`).
```

title: Bump golang.org/x/net to HEAD for http2 configureServer ALPN fix
author: dims
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Bumps `golang.org/x/net` from `v0.55.0` to `v0.55.1-0.20260602153038-42abb857022c` (master HEAD) to pick up the two go1.27 net/http http2 "wrap" fixes:

- https://go-review.googlesource.com/c/net/+/782940 — `configureServer` registers the `h2` / `http/1.1` ALPN protocols on `s.TLSConfig` (golang/go#79642).
- https://go-review.googlesource.com/c/net/+/785900 — `ConfigureTransport` / `ConfigureTransports` enable net/http's native HTTP/2 on the transport and keep `TLSClientConfig` non-nil (golang/go#79778).

Under go1.27, `golang.org/x/net/http2` becomes a thin wrapper over net/http's native HTTP/2. Before these fixes, the wrapped `ConfigureServer` and `ConfigureTransport(s)` no longer advertised/enabled HTTP/2 for callers that pass a custom `TLSConfig` / `TLSClientConfig` — which is exactly how the kube-apiserver secure-serving path and the client-go transport (`SetTransportDefaults`) are configured. HTTP/2 silently degraded to HTTP/1.1 on Go tip, surfacing as failures in `ci-kubernetes-unit-golang-tip` / `pull-kubernetes-e2e-unit-golang-tip` (apiserver goaway/graceful-termination/auth tests and `k8s.io/client-go/transport`).

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

xref kubernetes/kubernetes#139263, golang/go#79642, golang/go#79778

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Only `go.mod` / `go.sum` / `vendor/` change; the sole vendored source delta is under `vendor/golang.org/x/net/http2/`. Produced with `hack/pin-dependency.sh golang.org/x/net 42abb857022c` followed by `hack/update-vendor.sh`. Verified locally on both go1.26 and go1.27 (tip): the previously-failing apiserver and `client-go/transport` HTTP/2 tests pass with the original (un-modified) Kubernetes code.

author: yong-jie-gong
body:

5. If the PR is unfinished, see how to mark it: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#marking-unfinished-pull-requests
-->

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
When `distribute-cpus-across-numa` policy option is enabled, CPUManager's  `takeByTopologyNUMADistributed` function finds the **minimum** number of NUMA  nodes needed to satisfy a CPU request and distributes evenly across them.   However, when TopologyManager has explicitly selected a multi-NUMA affinity   (e.g., all 4 NUMA nodes because GPUs/NICs span them all), CPUManager ignores  this intent and shrinks the allocation back to fewer NUMA nodes.
     This PR ensures CPUManager honors the TopologyManager's NUMA affinity as a minimum constraint for distribution, preserving device topology alignment

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
<!--
Please link relevant issues to help with tracking.

To automatically close the linked issue(s) when this PR is merged,
add the word "Fixes" before the issue number or link.
Do not use "Fixes" if the PR is of kind `failing-test` or `flake`.

Reference KEPs when applicable in addition to specific issues.

Examples:

<issue link> (issue in a different repository)
KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/<kep-issue-number>

If there is no associated issue, then write "N/A".
-->
Fixes #139430 

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
1. `allocateCPUs()` now passes `numaAffinity.Count()` (number of NUMA nodes in the TopologyManager hint) through to `takeByTopologyNUMADistributed()`
2. `takeByTopologyNUMADistributed()` uses this as a floor for `minNUMAs`, the loop variable that controls the minimum combination size to try

The fix is conservative:
- Only applies when `distribute-cpus-across-numa` is enabled
- Only when a valid NUMA affinity hint exists (`numaAffinity != nil`)
- Falls back to original behavior if hint count exceeds available NUMA nodes
- Passes `0` (no constraint) for non-aligned allocation paths
####

closes.title: CPUManager shrinks multi-NUMA TopologyManager affinity when distributing exclusive CPUs across NUMA

title: Fix job controller reporting active=0 during pod creation backoff
author: akhilsingh-git
body:
<!--
Thanks for sending a pull request! Here are some tips for you:
-->

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind regression
/sig apps

#### What this PR does / why we need it

When the Job controller's manageJob() needs to create replacement pods but defers creation because a pod-failure backoff is still active, it returned a hardcoded active=0 to the caller. Since no pods were actually created or deleted, this left status.active=0 while status.ready still reflected the running pods.

The apiserver rejects such an update with a 422 (cannot set more ready pods than active). That failed update then blocks the controller from flushing uncounted terminated pods, removing finalizers, and updating job status — leaving pods stuck Terminating with stale status.

Both backoff early-returns (the global path and the per-index backoffLimitPerIndex path) now return the real active count. Regression tests are added for both paths.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Fixes #139428

#### Special notes for your reviewer

This became visible as 422 errors only after the ready <= active validation was introduced in 1.31 alongside managedBy reaching Beta — hence /kind regression.

```release-note
Fixed a regression in default 1.32+ configurations where the Job controller could attempt to report `status.active` as 0 while replacement Pod creation was deferred due to pod-failure backoff, causing the Job status update to be rejected by the apiserver. This could delay flushing uncounted terminated Pods, finalizer removal, and Job status updates, leaving Pods stuck `Terminating` and the Job with stale status until the backoff elapsed.
```

closes.title: Job controller manageJob() returns active=0 during backoff, causing "cannot set more ready pods than active" status update rejection

title: DRA kubelet: add v1 DRAResourceHealth gRPC API
author: harche
body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind cleanup
/kind api-change

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Promotes the DRAResourceHealth kubelet gRPC API from v1alpha1 to v1 (same proto) and moves all in-tree usage over. The beta package name is skipped, following the convention of other kubelet gRPC APIs.

Drivers no longer implement the versioned gRPC interface. They implement the new `WatchHealthStatus` method on the `DRAPlugin` interface using plain Go types, and the kubeletplugin helper does the gRPC serving: both v1 and v1alpha1 by default, so drivers work with kubelets 1.36 and older out of the box. The kubelet prefers v1 and, for three releases of transition (1.37 through 1.39), still consumes v1alpha1 from drivers which shipped before v1 existed. Both v1alpha1 paths get removed in the 1.40 era. The kubelet only opens the health stream for plugins that advertise the service.

Tried out in kubernetes-sigs/dra-example-driver#127 and kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu#1243, the latter on an NVIDIA L4 with both a released v1.36 kubelet (v1alpha1 path) and a kubelet built from this PR.

AI usage - AI was used during testing the example driver and nvidia driver and fixing minor issues found during that testing.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Fixes #139475
KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4680

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
The DRAResourceHealth kubelet gRPC API has been promoted to v1; the schema is unchanged from v1alpha1. `DRAPlugin.WatchHealthStatus` is a new mandatory method on the `k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/kubeletplugin` helper's `DRAPlugin` interface, replacing the optional versioned gRPC interface (one-time Go API break, existing drivers must add the method to compile). Drivers without health support return `ErrHealthNotSupported` from it or disable the service with `HealthService(false)`. The helper serves both v1 and v1alpha1 by default, so drivers report health on kubelets 1.36 and older without extra configuration. The kubelet prefers v1 and, for three releases of transition, still consumes v1alpha1 from drivers which shipped before v1 existed. The v1alpha1 DRAResourceHealth API is deprecated and gets removed in the 1.40 era. The kubelet only opens the device health stream for plugins that advertise the service.
```

```docs
- [KEP]: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4680
```

/kind regression
-->
/kind flake
/sig node

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This fixes a flaky e2e_node test for terminating a pod while it is still initializing restartable init containers.

The test deletes a pod with a 3 second grace period and asserts that the pod disappears in less than `grace + 2s`. It previously used `WaitForPodNotFoundInNamespace`, which uses the default e2e polling interval of 2 seconds. That polling interval is too coarse for a wall-clock assertion with only a 2 second buffer.

In the observed failure, kubelet did not hang waiting for restartable init containers that had not started. Kubelet removed the pod from etcd about 4.6 seconds after observing deletion, but the test reported about 6.1 seconds because it observed the final `NotFound` only on the next coarse poll.

This PR changes this specific test to wait for `NotFound` with a 100ms polling interval while preserving the existing 120 second timeout. The assertion now measures pod deletion latency instead of framework polling jitter.

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:
/kind api-change

/kind failing-test
/kind flake
/kind regression
-->
/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Migrates the toleration key format check (format=k8s-label-key) from handwritten validation to declarative validation.

`Toleration.Key` is tagged on the shared `core/v1.Toleration` type, so the rule applies to every type that embeds it — `PodSpec.tolerations` and `RuntimeClass.scheduling.tolerations` directly, and `Deployment/DaemonSet/ReplicaSet/StatefulSet/Job/CronJob/ReplicationController/PodTemplate` via the pod template. The handwritten error is marked covered by declarative validation.

Notable points for the shared validator (ValidateTolerations):
  - The covered marking is opt-in via a `KeyFormatCovered` option, so it applies only to the structured fields. Annotation-encoded tolerations (ValidateTolerationsInPodAnnotations) have no declarative counterpart and stay authoritative.
  - Adding the rule makes the workload types declarative-validation roots, so `+k8s:supportsSubresource="/scale"` is declared on the scalable apps types (matching ReplicationController) for the parent-update path that runs on `/scale`.

author: vishalanarase
body:
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:

1. If this is your first time, please read our contributor guidelines: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/first-contribution.md#your-first-contribution and developer guide https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/development.md#development-guide

4. If you want *faster* PR reviews, read how: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#best-practices-for-faster-reviews
5. If the PR is unfinished, see how to mark it: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#marking-unfinished-pull-requests
-->

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When rolling updates are enabled, the DRA kubelet plugin helper names the plugin registration socket `{driver_name}-{pod_uid}-reg.sock`. With the default registry path (`/var/lib/kubelet/plugins_registry`) and a 36-character pod UID, only ~30 characters remain for the driver name to stay within the 108-byte AF_UNIX path limit on Linux.

Drivers using common `*.sigs.k8s.io` names (for example `gpu.dra-example-driver.sigs.k8s.io`, 34 characters) fail to start during rolling updates with:

```listen unix .../gpu.dra-example-driver.sigs.k8s.io-<uid>-reg.sock: bind: invalid argument```

This PR picks the rolling-update registration socket basename based on the full path length under the configured `RegistrarDirectoryPath`. It tries, in order:

1. `<driver name>-<pod UID>-reg.sock` - preferred when it fits (keeps full UID for debugging)
2. `<driver name>-<base64(SHA-256(pod UID)[:8])>-reg.sock` - keeps driver name, shortens the UID portion
3. `dra-<base64(SHA-256(driver name, NUL, pod UID)[:16])>-reg.sock` - shortest fallback for very long driver names

For #139166's 34-character driver at the default registry path, tier 2 is used so the driver name stays visible in the socket path.

Non-rolling-update behavior is unchanged (`<driver name>-reg.sock`). Explicit `RegistrarSocketFilename` and `RollingUpdate` remain mutually exclusive.

title: Generalize memorymanager checkpoint
author: lukaszwojciechowski
body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

##### Why

Latest introduction of PodLevelResourceManagers feature gate to memory manager (and CPU manager) checkpoints, has made future enhancements of checkpoint structure barely possible.

Depending if PodLevelResourceManagers is enabled or not V1 or V2 versions of checkpoints are used.
So new feature X that would like to modify checkpoint is blocked. It would require 4 versions to be possible: when both of features (X and PodLevelResourceManagers) are enabled, when only one is, and when none is.

Because PodLevelResourceManagers was already merged and is part of 1.36 Kubernetes release,
this change needs to introduce new version V3 and provide smooth migration from old versions

##### What it does

This PR generalizes the memory manager checkpoint functionality by keeping data serialized to a string, which is a pattern used in DRA checkpoints. and applied already to CPU manager (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139102)

Instead of directly serializing the checkpoint struct, the actual checkpoint data is now stored in a separate struct which gets serialized to a string. The main checkpoint struct now contains this serialized data and a checksum of it.

This approach provides better forward/backward compatibility as the data structure can evolve without breaking existing checkpoints. It also allows for more robust error handling as deserialization issues can be caught and handled more gracefully.

The checksum is now calculated on the serialized data string rather than the struct itself, making it more reliable and consistent. File consistency is still kept as the checksum verification ensures data integrity.

Generalized checkpoint serialization is used regardless of feature gate settings. This allows future development of the checkpoint structure and enhancements for future features possible.

Additionally, V1 structure is embedded inline for forward compatibility - allowing older kubelet versions (using V1) to read newer V3 checkpoint files.

#### What type of PR is this?
/kind regression
