title: iscsi: keep detaching block volume when the by-path link is gone
author: abhinav-phi
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it

`DetachBlockISCSIDisk` returned an error when the `/dev/disk/by-path/ip-<portal>-iscsi-<iqn>-lun-<n>` symlink for the volume was already missing — which is exactly the state left behind when the iSCSI session is lost while a block-mode pod is still running and teardown happens afterwards:

```
kubelet[...]: Error: failed to validate devicePath: /dev/disk/by-path/ip-<portal>-iscsi-<iqn>-lun-0
```

Every retry failed the same way, the operation never reached its own logout step, and the volume stayed in `node.status.volumesInUse` until kubelet was restarted — during which any pod trying to attach the volume on another node got `Multi-Attach error ... Volume is already exclusively attached to one node`.

Three observations from the issue and verified in the code:

1. `devicePath` is not used after the check — it is computed, logged at V(5), stat'd, and discarded; the detach below uses `portals`, `iqn`, `iface`, `volName`, `initiatorName`.
2. The steps it protects already handle a missing session: `detachISCSIDisk` wraps logout and node-record delete in `ignoreExitCodes(err, exit_ISCSI_ERR_NO_OBJS_FOUND, exit_ISCSI_ERR_SESS_NOT_FOUND)`, and `isSessionBusy` counts plugin directories (portal-iqn prefixed dirs) rather than devices, so the missing link does not affect it.
3. The filesystem-mode equivalent `DetachDisk` performs the same `PathExists` early return, portal/IQN extraction, `isSessionBusy` guard and `detachISCSIDisk` call with no device check at all.

This PR logs the missing link (V(4)) and continues, making the block path behave like the filesystem path. Other `os.Stat` failures (permissions, I/O errors, ...) still abort the detach with an error.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Fixes #141839

#### Special notes for your reviewer

- Added `TestDetachBlockISCSIDiskMissingDevicePath`: it sets up the plugin `volumeDevices/iface-<iface>/<portal>-<iqn>-lun-0` dir with a persisted `iscsi.json`, no `/dev/disk/by-path` link (none exists in the test environment), and a scripted fake `iscsiadm`. It asserts `DetachBlockISCSIDisk` completes and reaches both the logout and the node-record delete calls. Against the old code it fails with `failed to validate devicePath`.
- Verified against a real cluster by the issue reporter (v1.33.13 with the equivalent change): teardown completed and both volumes left `volumesInUse` on their own.
- The check dates to a6d979dd88 (block volume support) and has been dead-prone since; no release note gating beyond the bugfix one below.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed an issue where the in-tree iSCSI detach of a block volume could fail permanently when the /dev/disk/by-path link was already gone (e.g. the iSCSI session was lost before teardown), leaving the volume stuck in node.status.volumesInUse and blocking attach on other nodes.
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhanceme

closes.title: in-tree iSCSI: DetachBlockISCSIDisk fails permanently when the by-path link is already gone, stranding the volume in volumesInUse

title: test: remove tCtx.Cancel workarounds
author: pohly
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Since https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141545, a TContext created by ktesting.Init is automatically canceled as soon as the test binary considers the test done, before any t.Cleanup callback runs. Previously, many tests had to explicitly call tCtx.Cancel(...) at the end of the test (typically via defer) to stop tCtx-driven background goroutines (controllers, informers, schedulers) because automatic cancellation only happened during Cleanup, i.e. too late. That workaround is now redundant and is removed throughout the codebase.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Three different patterns had to be handled, depending on what the removed Cancel call was ordering:

 - Bare "defer tCtx.Cancel(...)" with nothing else depending on it: simply deleted. This wasn't necessary in the first place.

 - "tCtx.Cancel(...)" followed by dependent code in the same defer/closure (e.g. wg.Wait(), informerFactory.Shutdown(), runtime.WaitForShutdown()): kept the dependent code but moved it (without the Cancel call) into tCtx.Cleanup(...), since Cleanup callbacks now reliably run only after the automatic cancellation.

 - "tCtx.Cancel(...)" was ordering a *separate* deferred teardown function (e.g. "defer closeFn()" or "defer server.TearDownFn()") registered *earlier* in the same function. Because Go defers run LIFO, the old code relied on Cancel (registered later) running before that teardown (registered earlier), guaranteeing tCtx-driven goroutines stopped before the apiserver they talk to was torn down. Simply deleting the Cancel call would break this ordering: the deferred teardown would now run immediately when the test function returns, while the goroutine keeps running unconstrained until the (now later) automatic cancellation during Cleanup - risking connection errors or a "Log in goroutine after Test has completed" panic. These sites were fixed by converting the deferred teardown into a t.Cleanup/tCtx.Cleanup registration.

   In some cases the teardown can be removed entirely by directly registering the corresponding operation inside the setup function.

Left untouched: Cancel calls used for legitimate mid-test, explicit timing (e.g. servicecidr's migration test cancels the first controller before switching to a second apiserver), and self-contained helpers that synchronously call Cancel as their own first action regardless of ktesting's automatic timing (e.g. resourceclaim's stopInformers, invoked both via defer and explicitly mid-test).


#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
NONE
```

#### AI usage disclosure:

YES. I explained how to remove explicit cancel calls and an agent did the work. I reviewed.

title: Automated cherry pick of #141307: DRA: avoid integer overflow in per-claim device-limit checks
author: thc1006
body:
Cherry pick of #141307 on release-1.37.

#141307: DRA: avoid integer overflow in per-claim device-limit checks

For details on the cherry pick process, see the [cherry pick requests](https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-release/cherry-picks.md) page.

#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it
Backports the per-claim device-limit overflow fix. The pre-flight loop in `Allocate` sums each request's device count into `minDevicesPerClaim` as a native `int`, and `allocateOne` builds `len(results) + numDevices - deviceIndex` the same way. Two `ExactCount` requests of `math.MaxInt/2 + 1` wrap the sum negative, so the `> AllocationResultsMaxSize` check is false and the negative total goes on to size the result slice.

Reaching it takes no feature gate. `DeviceRequest.Count` is validated only as `> 0`, and all three allocator variants on this branch carry the unguarded arithmetic, so whichever one a feature configuration selects is affected.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes
Backport of #141307, which fixes #141323 on master. pohly asked for the cherry pick there, then reopened #141323 with the condition that it stays open until 1.34 through 1.37 all carry the fix. The full set is #141922 for release-1.37, #141923 for release-1.36, #141924 for release-1.35 and #141925 for release-1.34.

Clean cherry-pick, no conflicts. The diff is identical to the master change apart from the blob hashes: same four files, same per-file line counts, and the whole patch matches line for line including the hunk offsets.

I built release-1.37 with the change and ran `go test ./staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/structured/...`, all green.

Reverting the three production files and keeping the tests, on this branch:

```
--- FAIL: TestAllocator (0.01s)

        allocator_incubating.go:167: I0908 12:02:16.979629] Starting allocation numClaims=1 numSlicesForNode=0
        allocator_incubating.go:178: I0908 12:02:16.980185] Gathered pool information pools={"content":[],"count":0,"devices":null}
        allocator_incubating.go:267: I0908 12:02:16.980244] Checked claim claim="claim-0" minDevices=-9223372036854775808
        allocator_incubating.go:169: I0908 12:02:16.980268] Done with allocation success=false err=null
panic: runtime error: makeslice: cap out of range [recovered, repanicked]
```

The stack is trimmed there; the frame is `incubating.(*Allocator).Allocate` at `allocator_incubating.go:277`. `minDevices=-9223372036854775808` is the wrapped sum. The stable and experimental variants panic the same way.

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR refactors the PodGroup preemption code to allow injecting custom code for victim ordering/grouping and preemption actuation.

This is needed for scheduler-library to allow Kueue to inject their own victims and to simulate preemption without actuating it. We still want to keep most of the PodGroup preemption logic.

This change is only supposed to open up the possibility for customization. The logic used by the scheduler should remain unchanged by this PR. However, a couple of small changes sneaked in:

1. The order of the final candidate victims is changed in case there are both violating and non-violating victims. This will impact lastVictim in actuation, however I didn't see any functional impact from it
2. The function result changes in case the preemptor is waiting for pods to be removed and has PreemptNever policy. Previously it would return Unschedulable, now it will return Success. This is an edge case, and it should eventually result in Unschedulable (once the preemption finalizes).

This change may impact performance. Previous logic contained early returns that could save us from computing the PDB violations or sorting the victims. However, I expect this impact to be insignificant, as the main bottleneck is running the scheduling function. Local runs of scheduler_perf don't show regression.

title: kubelet: reject unknown seccomp profile types
author: saschagrunert
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The `fieldSeccompProfile` function used an if-chain that silently fell through to `Unconfined` for any unrecognized `SeccompProfileType`. This means an unknown type would run the container without seccomp protection and without any error.

This replaces the if-chain with a switch that explicitly handles all three valid types (`Unconfined`, `RuntimeDefault`, `Localhost`) and returns an error for anything else.

An empty `Type` is also rejected now, where it previously fell through to `Unconfined`. API validation requires the type, and the kubelet runs the same validation for static pods, so nothing valid reaches this code path with an empty type.

The error message for a `Localhost` profile without `localhostProfile` loses its trailing period, which is visible in the pod event text.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/6061

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

This is a prerequisite for KEP-6061 (OCI Artifact Security Profiles). The version skew strategy in that KEP requires this fix so that older kubelets fail closed on new profile types (like the future `OCI` type) rather than silently falling through to `Unconfined`.

The API validation layer (`validateSeccompProfileType`) already rejects unknown types at admission, so this is defense-in-depth at the kubelet runtime level. The AppArmor handler already fails closed on unknown types; this brings seccomp in line with that behavior.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
kubelet: a Pod with an unknown or empty `seccompProfile.type` now fails closed, the container fails to start with `CreateContainerConfigError` instead of silently running as `Unconfined`. Both values are already rejected by API validation on Pod create and update, and by the kubelet's own validation for static Pods, so no Pod accepted by a supported API server is affected. This only changes behavior for Pods that reached the kubelet without passing API validation, or for a kubelet older than an API server that supports a seccomp profile type the kubelet does not know. The error message for a `Localhost` profile without `localhostProfile` no longer ends with a trailing period.
```

title: Fix ResourceFieldSelector.Divisor doc: unset or 0 means unscaled
author: kr-ravindra
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind documentation

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The doc comment on `ResourceFieldSelector.Divisor` says the field "defaults to 1". It does not: there is no server-side defaulting for the field, so an object written without a divisor is read back with an explicit `0`. Only when the value is consumed do the helpers treat an unset or `0` divisor as `1` (a divisor of 0 is meaningless). The mismatch between the comment and the persisted value has confused users of GitOps tooling that diffs live objects against manifests.

This updates the comment in `pkg/apis/core/types.go` and `staging/src/k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go` to the wording the API approver proposed in the issue, describing both meanings, and regenerates the derived docs (protobuf comments, swagger doc strings, applyconfigurations, OpenAPI specs). The approver preferred a documentation fix over changing defaulting or serialization, since that would make consecutive API server versions default and serialize the same persisted resource differently.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #128865

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

@soltysh, pinging you per your offer in the issue to shepherd this through. This is a comment-only change with regenerated docs; no API behaviour, defaulting, validation, or serialization changes. The change was drafted with an AI coding agent under my direction; I reviewed the diff and ran the generators and verify scripts.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
NONE
```

title: DRA kubeletplugin: shorten rolling service socket paths
author: ryo-whaletech
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig node
/wg device-management

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

With `RollingUpdate`, the DRA kubelet plugin helper normally uses `dra-<Pod UID>.sock` for the automatic service socket. The default plugin directory also contains the full driver name, so a valid 37-byte driver name makes the full endpoint exactly 108 bytes and therefore unusable as a pathname-based AF_UNIX socket.

This change preserves `dra-<Pod UID>.sock` whenever the full path fits. If it would exceed the AF_UNIX limit, the helper switches to a deterministic shortened basename containing 64 bits of the Pod UID's SHA-256 digest encoded with URL-safe, unpadded Base64. With the default directory and the maximum valid 63-byte driver name, the resulting endpoint is 104 bytes.

Non-rolling `dra.sock` naming, ordinary short-driver rolling naming, and explicit `PluginSocket` behavior remain unchanged. Arbitrary custom `PluginDataDirectoryPath` values are not guaranteed to fit.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #142002

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Related work is distinct: #139166 and #139623 addressed the rolling registration socket under `plugins_registry`; #139623 explicitly left `dra-<uid>.sock` service sockets unchanged. #141815 corrected the registration fallback's exact-108 boundary. #140837 added kubelet-side endpoint and driver validation, but does not prevent this helper from generating an invalid automatic service endpoint.

Verification on Kubernetes master `3af569e862d19a046cdfd63cda837f9bb29da6fa` with Go 1.27.1:

```console
go test ./staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/kubeletplugin -run='Test(RollingUpdatePluginSocketPathLength|PluginSocketAutomaticNaming|RollingUpdatePluginSocketFile_distinctInputs)$' -count=1

go test -race ./staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/kubeletplugin -count=1
go vet ./staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/kubeletplugin
gofmt -d staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/kubeletplugin/draplugin.go staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/kubeletplugin/draplugin_test.go
git diff --check
```

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed DRA kubelet plugin helper rolling updates for drivers with long valid names by shortening automatic DRA service socket paths when needed.
```


title: ktesting: fix auto-cancellation
author: pohly
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Init cancels its TContext automatically when the test ends, via runWhenDone (context.AfterFunc on the test's own context). withTB, used by TContext.Run for sub-tests, never set this up, so a sub-test's TContext was only canceled when the whole parent test finished, not when that sub-test itself ended. Found when using the new ktesting semantic more widely.

SyncTest has a related but distinct problem: even with the above fixed, automatic cancellation via context.AfterFunc runs the callback in a new goroutine, but synctest checks for durably blocked goroutines the instant the bubble's main goroutine returns, with no guarantee that the AfterFunc goroutine ran in time. Fixed by canceling synchronously via defer around the callback instead.

Besides these fixes in ktesting itself, some tests also hadn't been fully updated to handle the revised semantic - see commits.

title: node: graduate RuntimeClass declarative validation to stable
author: krishhna24
body:
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you: -->

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Graduates RuntimeClass's declarative validation from beta to stable, per KEP-5073, and deletes the handwritten validation it replaces.

The `handler` field carries three rules, identically in v1, v1alpha1 and v1beta1:

```
+k8s:format="k8s-short-name"
+k8s:immutable
+k8s:required
```

Dropping the `+k8s:beta(since: "1.37")=` wrapper makes them enforced without `DeclarativeValidationBeta`. The generator's only output change is that `.MarkBeta()` is no longer appended to the `validate.X(...)` calls.

The three handwritten checks in `pkg/apis/node/validation/validation.go` are deleted in the same commit. That is not a stylistic choice: `FilterCoveredHandwrittenErrors` suppresses a handwritten error only while a matching *beta* declarative error is enforced, so a stable rule that kept its twin would report the violation twice and drive `apiserver_validation_declarative_validation_mismatch_total` non-zero. Keeping them separable is not possible.

They pair 1:1, each already carrying the matching origin:

| rule | handwritten twin |
|---|---|
| `+k8s:required` | `validation.go:48`, `field.Required(...)` |
| `+k8s:format="k8s-short-name"` | `validation.go:51`, `WithOrigin("format=k8s-short-name")` |
| `+k8s:immutable` | `validation.go:69`, `WithOrigin("immutable")` |

All three versions are registered in `pkg/apis/node/install/install.go`, so `VerifyVersionedValidationEquivalence` covers the group even though only `nodev1` is served.

Follows #141533, the agreed example PR for this wave. One API type, as asked for on the tracking issue.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Part of #141532

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Deleting the handwritten checks removes exactly three unit test cases in `validation_test.go` that existed only to exercise them: `invalid Handler name`, `invalid empty RuntimeClass` and `invalid Handler update`. Before deleting them I confirmed they fail for the right reason, i.e. the three deletions produce exactly those three failures and nothing else moves. The declarative suite covers the same ground and keeps its cases, minus `.MarkBeta()` on the expected errors.

Verified locally:

```
go test ./test/declarative_validation/node/...   # all three gate configs pass
go test ./pkg/apis/node/... ./pkg/api/testing/...
hack/verify-codegen.sh                           # exit 0
```

title: e2e podlogs: fix handling of network issues
author: pohly
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup
/kind failing-test
/kind flake

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The Pods watch loop had two issues when the apiserver becomes temporarily unreachable:
- the periodic ticker case did not call check(), so a missed watch event was never noticed
- once the watch's result channel closed, receiving from it never blocks again, causing a busy loop of reconnect/List calls

Fix both by using a RetryWatcher, which reconnects with a minimum delay between attempts, and by calling check() from the ticker case.

The TestCopyPodLogsAPIServerTemporarilyDown integration test covers this scenario. Without the fix, the test fails with:

    podlogs_test.go:182: FATAL ERROR: I0914 17:38:30.045924]

title: DRA testing: separate creation of counters and capacity
author: pohly
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Counters (from the partitionable devices feature) and capacity (original device attribute for use in CEL, extended by consumable capacity) are different concepts. Lumping them together when constructing test slices via `fromCounters` made tests hard to understand because helpers had unexpected behavior. It also wasn't clear that withCapacityRequest is a request for one particular capacity.

Counters are not qualified. Using the same names for capacities led to tests for consumable capacity which don't cover using fully-qualified names and probably contributed to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/140650.

Counters and capacity names are now clearly separated. All capacity gets declared explicitly if (and only if) needed. Several test cases created slices with capacity without doing anything with it. Those now use simpler slices.

The new `withAttribute` and `withCapacity` helpers replace passing attributes and capacity to the device constructor. They simplify writing test cases because they remove the need for constructing maps and pointers. The same could also be done elsewhere, but that's left for later.

title: hpa: exclude pod overhead from pod-level request calculations
author: sophieliu15
body:
When evaluating pod-level resource requests in `calculatePodLevelRequests`, `ReplicaCalculator` previously passed an uninitialized `PodResourcesOptions`, defaulting `ExcludeOverhead` to `false`. This included `pod.spec.overhead` in the request denominator, depressing calculated utilization for sandboxed workloads and breaking parity with container-level calculations that do not include overhead.

This change sets `ExcludeOverhead` to `true` so that pod-level and container-level request evaluations remain consistent with container cgroup metrics.

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
When evaluating pod-level resource requests in `calculatePodLevelRequests`, `ReplicaCalculator` previously passed an uninitialized `resourcehelpers.PodResourcesOptions{}`, which defaults `ExcludeOverhead` to `false`. As a result, `resourcehelpers.PodRequests` included `pod.spec.overhead` in the request calculation.
This causes two issues in HPA:
1. **Metric Boundary Mismatch:** HPA calculates utilization as `∑ Usage(p) / ∑ Request(p)`. The usage metrics scraped by metrics-server/Kubelet (`/metrics/resource`) measure container cgroups only (`cri-containerd-<CID>.scope`). Sandbox runtime overhead (e.g. Kata Containers, gVisor) runs outside container cgroups in the pod sandbox slice and is not included in container usage metrics. Adding overhead to the request denominator artificially lowers calculated utilization and delays scale-up.
2. **Asymmetry with Container Requests:** When pod-level resources are not specified, `calculatePodRequestsFromContainers` sums container requests and never includes `pod.spec.overhead`. Workloads configured with pod-level resources should evaluate compute utilization identically to workloads configured with container requests.

title: limitranger: skip min/max on an unchanged PVC request on update
author: thc1006
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

LimitRanger checks a PersistentVolumeClaim against the min and max of the LimitRange on create and on every update, and it has only ever looked at the new object (#30145). A request that was accepted when the claim was stored, or that a LimitRange created later no longer allows, fails every update of that claim, even one that only touches labels. #141348 made the comparison exact, which added the requests that used to pass only because both sides were rounded to whole units. For a bound claim the request cannot go down to `status.capacity` or below, so when the max is at or under the capacity nothing satisfies both.

This passes the stored object into `ValidateLimit` and skips the min and max checks for a request that the update leaves as stored. A request that is changed, added or removed is still checked, and so is every other resource in the range and every create. Both objects must have the request and `Cmp` must report the values equal for it to count as unchanged, so `20Gi` and `20480Mi` are one value. It is the ratcheting rule from #141166, and the reasoning #62673 applied to pod updates in 2018.

The test goes through `Validate` with real admission attributes, old and new object included, and each error case checks the exact message, so it also shows which constraint fired. The cases are the rows of the ratcheting table: create, unchanged, changed, added and removed, each on both sides of the range where that applies. With the skip taken out, five cases fail: the four that keep a stored request outside the range, and the one that adds a second resource next to an unchanged one.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Part of #141166

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

This only covers PVCs. Pod updates through the `resize` subresource are in #142171, and `ValidateResourceQuotaUpdate` still checks every entry of `spec.hard`. An apiserver without this change keeps rejecting such an update, so a skewed rollout is no worse than master. `LimitRangerActions` is only implemented by `DefaultLimitRangerActions` in the tree. The LimitRange page on kubernetes.io says an update that violates a constraint is rejected, so I'll send a docs change once this settles.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
LimitRanger no longer rejects an update of a PersistentVolumeClaim because of a request that the update leaves unchanged, even when that request is outside the LimitRange minimum or maximum. A changed, added or removed request is checked against both the minimum and the maximum, as on create, so a stored request outside the range is rejected as soon as an update changes it.
```

```docs

```

The change and the test were drafted with an AI assistant. I reviewed and edited them and ran the tests and linters myself.

title: limitranger: skip unchanged pod resources on resize
author: semx
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

On a resize, LimitRanger runs `PodValidateLimitFunc` against the whole pod again: every container, every init container, and the pod-level totals. None of that is scoped to what the resize changed, so a stored value that no longer satisfies a constraint gets rejected on an update that did not touch it. Init containers are included: on master any of them can be resized (`InPlacePodVerticalScalingInitContainers` has defaulted on since v1.36 and is GA and locked on since v1.37), so they are just more containers a resize may or may not have touched.

This follows the ratcheting rule from #141166: a value the stored object already holds is valid by definition. The stored pod is now passed into `PodValidateLimitFunc`, and a check is skipped when the value is unchanged:

- Container level: for a container resource, when both the request and the limit match the container of the same name in the stored pod. Both fields are compared because each of the min, max and ratio constraints reads both the request and the limit. Init containers go through the same check as regular containers.
- Pod level: for a resource, when the pod requests and limits totals match the stored pod's, computed with the same options. This is deliberately about the totals: the pod-type constraint applies to the total, and an unchanged total is the stored one, even when two containers moved in opposite directions. Each of those containers is still checked at the container level.

Anything the resize changes is checked exactly as on create, and create is unchanged (no stored pod, nothing is skipped). The two identical per-container loops are folded into one helper so the skip is applied in one place.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Part of #141166 (LimitRanger line, pod resize side). #142170 added the `oldObj` plumbing and covers the PVC side; this wires the pod branch of `ValidateLimit` that it left unchanged.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

`TestLimitRangerValidatePodResize` goes through the real `Validate` with the old and new pod on the `resize` subresource, 19 cases: an unchanged container above the max and a resized one above it; an unchanged init container below the min and a resized restartable init container above the max; a cpu resize that leaves the same container's unchanged memory alone; a resize that lowers only the request below the min; an unchanged second container next to a resized one; unchanged and changed pod totals against min and max, and the same for pod-level resources with `PodLevelResources` on; unchanged and changed limit-to-request ratios at the container level and at the pod level; offsetting resizes that leave the pod total unchanged; a resize that adds a limit the stored container did not have (checked, since presence changed); and create being checked in full.

Mutation (`PodMutateLimitFunc`) is not touched; defaulting on resize is unchanged.

Dropped

title: core/validation: keep stored ResourceQuota values out of update checks
author: thc1006
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`ValidateResourceQuotaUpdate` checks the whole new `spec.hard`, and the status update checks every `status.hard` and `status.used` value, without looking at the stored object. The integer check for those values became stricter in c09332890d6. A value past the milli range that the wrapped milli projection used to accept is rejected now, so a quota that stores one cannot be updated at all, not even to change a label. A v1.31 apiserver accepted `spec.hard[pods]: 18446744073709551616m`, because the milli projection wrapped to 0, and the test added with that commit records the lock-out as current behavior.

This compares each value with the one the object already stores under the same key and skips the value checks when the two are equal. Equal means `Quantity.Cmp` returns 0, the comparison the semantic equality for quantities uses. Names are still checked for every entry, scopes and the scope selector as before, and a create is checked in full. A value the update adds or changes is checked as on create. `spec.hard` is compared with the stored `spec.hard`, `status.used` with the stored `status.used`, and `status.hard` with the stored `status.hard` or the stored `spec.hard`. The quota controller writes `spec.hard` into `status.hard` whenever the two differ, and admission enforces `status.hard`. A status the controller cannot write would leave the quota with an empty or stale limit. Only the integer check has changed over time, and a negative value could not have been stored, so nothing new gets in this way.

The test that pinned the lock-out now pins this behavior, with the fractional fixture from that commit and the update and status cases around it.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Related to #141166 (validation compatibility row, ResourceQuota part)

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

An older apiserver in a mixed-version control plane rejects the same update, as it does today. ResourceQuota has no declarative validation tags, so there is no second copy of these rules to keep in step.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
ResourceQuota updates no longer fail validation on a `spec.hard`, `status.hard` or `status.used` value that the object already holds, so a quota holding a value an older release accepted can still be updated and its status still synced.
```

title: HPA: compute resource utilization ratio without int64 overflow
author: kr-ravindra
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig autoscaling

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`GetResourceUtilizationRatio` sums per-pod metric values and requests as raw `int64`, multiplies the metrics total by 100 and narrows to `int32`. All three steps wrap silently. Near `math.MaxInt64` the HPA ends up with a `currentUtilization` of 0 and a negative raw average, and scales the wrong way or not at all.

The two totals are now accumulated exactly with `math/big`, the percentage is taken exactly, and only the final `int32` narrowing is clamped to `math.MaxInt32`/`math.MinInt32`, so an oversized utilization keeps its direction instead of wrapping. The raw average of `int64` values always fits an `int64`, so `rawAverageValue` is unchanged in type and meaning. `GetMetricUsageRatio` had the same unchecked sum and now accumulates the same way. Nothing changes for inputs that fit today and there is no new error path.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Related to #141166 (HPA row of the Quantity int64 overflow burndown; does not close the tracker)

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Continues #141978, which GitHub closed on a force-push and refuses to reopen; the two review comments from @jpbetz there (doc comment, and the exact sum in `GetMetricUsageRatio`) are addressed in this head. /cc @jpbetz

The `int32` narrowing saturates rather than returning an error, matching the direction-preserving cap taken for replica counts in #141397. If you would rather the HPA surface an error condition when the percentage does not fit, that is a two-line change and I am happy to make it.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed the HorizontalPodAutoscaler utilization and usage calculations wrapping to a wrong or negative current value when pod metric or request totals exceeded int64 or the utilization percentage exceeded int32; the reported percentage now saturates at the int32 limit.
```

title: core/validation: cover the ResourceQuota status.hard source fallback
author: thc1006
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

#142190 let a ResourceQuota update keep a `status.hard` value that the object already stores. The quota controller writes `spec.hard` into `status.hard` on every sync, and that check accepts a `status.hard` value equal to the stored `status.hard` or the stored `spec.hard`. The tests that went in with it start from an empty stored status, and the fallback to `spec.hard` is only reached when `status.hard` is absent.

This adds two cases to `TestValidateResourceQuotaUpdateKeepsStoredQuantities`. In the first, the stored `status.hard` is present but stale, and the update replaces it with the value from the stored `spec.hard` while usage advances. The match has to come from the spec, not the stale status. In the second, a `spec.hard` in the same request has the new value, and the validator must not use it as the source, because the source is the old object.

Both cases pass on master. Each one fails if the check is narrowed to the first source with the key, or if it reads the new spec instead of the stored one. Together they pin the part of #142190 the earlier tests left open.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Follow-up to #142190. Part of #141166.

title: DRA consumable capacity + CEL: fix name comparisons and lookup
author: pohly
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When the ResourceClaim requested "driver.example.com/bandwidth" and that DRA driver published the capacity as "bandwidth", the request failed. Same for the inverse case.

A less likely problem existed when a DRA driver flipped between publishing with and without its own driver name as prefix: the allocation result stored literally what came from the driver at the time of allocation, which then wouldn't be considered after flipping to the other format.

Nothing prevents DRA drivers and users from publishing resp. requesting the same capacity with and without driver name prefix. Validation could prevent this for ResourceSlices (driver name is known) but doesn't. It's probably also not worth doing because DRA drivers are trusted and  can trivially avoid this; validation would just add overhead. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142218 makes sure that DRA driver behave well.

Lookup for constraints resolves this conflict via "fully-qualified wins". Consumable capacity and CEL resolution was random (last one in map iteration wins), now also prefers fully-qualified.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/140650

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The fix is to normalize names (drop redundant prefix) before comparing. To support downgrades, the allocation result is written with the simpler name without the driver name as prefix because that is what was written in practice before.

I have included making the consumable capacities and CEL capacities/attributes lookup deterministic in this PR. The one about CEL could also be a separate PR, but it seems related enough to not add that review overhead.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
DRA consumable capacity: requesting capacity had to be done with the capacity name exactly as published by drivers, i.e. typically without the driver name prefix. When requesting with a fully-qualified name, the request failed. Now both unqualified and fully-qualified names work. A related, less likely problem existed when a DRA driver changed how it published capacity and some capacity was allocated already.
```

#### AI usage disclosure:

YES: test cases were written manually, then AI was used to fix the code based on a description what the solution should look like.

closes.title: DRA consumable capacity: validate as fully qualified name in capacity requests

title: Add Pod and PodStatus PATCH microbenchmarks
author: jefftree
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup
/sig api-machinery

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Adds microbenchmarks for the Pod `PATCH`, `PUT`, `POST` and `DELETE` write paths in `test/integration/apiserver/storage`, driving the apiserver handlers against a realistic Pod fixture backed by a real etcd.

The seeded Pod stores as 10,999 B of Protobuf, 11,125 B once a PATCH adds a managedFields entry. Allocation amplification against that size:

- `PATCH /pods` (`BenchmarkPatchPod`): 1,101,193 B/op (99.0x) and 16,803 allocs/op
- `PATCH /pods/status` (`BenchmarkPatchPodStatus`): 1,005,117 B/op (90.3x) and 15,414 allocs/op
- `PUT /pods` (`BenchmarkUpdatePod`): 895,941 B/op (80.5x) and 13,261 allocs/op
- `POST /pods` (`BenchmarkCreatePod`): 315,959 B/op (28.4x) and 4,124 allocs/op
- `DELETE /pods` (`BenchmarkDeletePod`): 493,911 B/op (44.4x) and 3,390 allocs/op

`BenchmarkUpdatePod` writes the same label as `BenchmarkPatchPod`, so the gap between them bounds what the strategic merge itself costs, about 19 percent of the request.

Storage is the real `etcd3.store` against the etcd process `framework.EtcdMain` already starts, via `framework.SharedEtcd()`. Because that etcd is a separate process, its bbolt and raft allocations are not counted, so `b.ReportAllocs()` still isolates the apiserver side. The counts do include the etcd clientv3 and gRPC request path, which is part of what a write costs.

Every write goes through the endpoint handlers, including the seeding, so `managedFields` are server-computed rather than supplied by the fixture. The benchmarks call `handlers.PatchResource` and friends directly rather than going through `StartTestServer`, so authn, authz and the admission chain stay out of the numbers.

```text
goos: linux
goarch: amd64
pkg: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/integration/apiserver/storage
cpu: Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU @ 2.80GHz
BenchmarkPatchPod-32          	     300	   6711054 ns/op	 1101193 B/op	   16803 allocs/op
BenchmarkPatchPodStatus-32    	     300	   6178954 ns/op	 1005117 B/op	   15414 allocs/op
BenchmarkUpdatePod-32         	     300	   6437344 ns/op	  895941 B/op	   13261 allocs/op
BenchmarkCreatePod-32         	     300	   3607992 ns/op	  315959 B/op	    4124 allocs/op
BenchmarkDeletePod-32         	     300	   5035822 ns/op	  493911 B/op	    3390 allocs/op
```

Median of 5 runs. ns/op is fsync bound here and noisy, the allocation columns are the stable signal.

Until kubelet completes registration and patches NodeStatus back to the API server, predicateAdmitHandler evaluates incoming static pods (e.g., kube-proxy) and early scheduled pods against zero allocatable resources, rejecting them with UnexpectedAdmissionError.

This commit updates getCachedNode and getNodeSync to ensure that if the v1.Node returned by the informer or API server has an uninitialized Status.Allocatable, kubelet does a reconciliation with a locally constructed initial node, and caches it.

title: job controller: clear expectations when deleting Job
author: 6democratickim9
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The Job controller tracks pending Pod creations and deletions by namespace/name. If a Job is deleted while a Pod creation is in flight and another Job is immediately created with the same name, the replacement can inherit the old Job's unsatisfied expectation. `syncJob` then skips `manageJob`, leaving the replacement unreconciled until another event or the expectations timeout.

This change clears Pod expectations from the Job delete-event handler, matching the existing behavior of the ReplicaSet and DaemonSet controllers.

It also adds a deterministic integration test. The test blocks the old Job's Pod POST after the creation expectation has been raised, deletes and recreates the Job under the same name with a new UID, waits for the informer to observe the replacement, and then releases the old request. It verifies that the replacement Job is reconciled and receives its suspended condition.

Without the fix, the test reproduces the stale-UID status error from the issue and times out waiting for the replacement Job:

```
Precondition failed: UID in precondition: <old UID>, UID in object meta: <new UID>
```

With the fix, the integration test passes.

I was assigned to #142142 on September 16 and started investigating the reproduction and integration coverage before #142236 was opened. #142236 implements the same expectation cleanup with unit coverage; this PR includes the integration reproduction requested in the issue discussion.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #142142

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Local verification:

- The new integration test fails on unmodified `master` with the stale-UID error and an unreconciled replacement Job.
- The new integration test passes three consecutive runs with this change.
- `go test ./pkg/controller/job/...` passes.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed an issue where a Job recreated with the same name as a recently deleted Job could remain unreconciled because it inherited pending Pod expectations from the previous Job.
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

```docs
NONE
```

#### AI usage disclosure:

AI assistance was used while investigating the controller flow and developing the integration test. I reviewed the changes and locally verified both the baseline failure and the fixed behavior using a real kube-apiserver and etcd.

title: kubelet: stabilize allocated resource health ordering
author: photoszzt
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Canonicalizes `AllocatedResourcesStatus` by resource name and each resource health list by resource ID in both the device manager and DRA manager. This prevents unchanged resource health from producing different serialized Pod statuses and unnecessary API updates.

Regression tests seed deliberately unsorted existing statuses, so the old behavior fails deterministically without relying on randomized map iteration.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #142293

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Focused race tests and the DRA package tests pass. The device-manager package passes with `TestDevicePluginReRegistrationProbeMode` excluded; that unrelated timing-sensitive test passes alone but can fail under parallel load.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Kubelet now reports allocated resource health statuses in deterministic order, preventing unnecessary Pod status updates when resource health is unchanged.
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

```docs
NONE
```

#### AI usage disclosure:

YES. AI assistance was used to trace the affected kubelet paths, implement deterministic ordering, and add regression coverage. The human author is responsible for reviewing all submitted changes in accordance with `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

title: Refactor PodGroupProtectionController to use namespacedKey and objectOf functions
author: jdzikowski
body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind cleanup
/sig scheduling
/wg workload-aware-scheduling
#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Refactors `pkg/controller/scheduling/podgroupprotection` to lay the groundwork for upcoming `CompositePodGroup` garbage collection protection (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141021):
- Introduces `namespacedKey(namespace, name string)` to standardize `namespace/name` key construction across indexers, event handlers, and lister lookups without `cache.MetaNamespaceKeyFunc` overhead.
- Replaces `getPod(obj interface{}) *v1.Pod` with a generic `objectOf[T any](<obj any>) T` helper that extracts typed objects directly or unwraps `cache.DeletedFinalStateUnknown` tombstones across informer event handlers.
- Updates `TestGetPod` to `TestObjectOf`.
#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Part of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141021
#### Special notes for your reviewer:
Split out from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141021 to keep the helper refactoring separate and easier to review.

title: e2e_node: restart kubelet once NodeUnprepareResources is in progress
author: thc1006
body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind flake
/sig node

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
The two-plugin test "must call NodeUnprepareResources again if it's in progress for one plugin when Kubelet restarts" restarts the kubelet right after both NodePrepareResources calls succeed. Nothing checks that the kubelet is inside plugin2's blocked NodeUnprepareResources at that point.

In the four failures on ci-node-crio-dra listed in [#142404](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/142404) the restart landed while the old kubelet's CreateContainer was still in flight. CRI-O logs `CreateCtr: context was either canceled or the deadline was exceeded`, the new kubelet creates the container again, the pod finishes, and StopPodSandbox then takes 118 to 119 s because the sandbox still holds the container that was created but never started. The kubelet calls NodeUnprepareResources only after that stop, later than the 120 s the test waits.

The passing runs show no cancelled CreateContainer and no long sandbox stop. The same early restart shows up on ci-node-e2e-containerd-2-0-dra-1-34 (run 2098416805084139520, 2026-09-11) with a different outcome: NodeUnprepareResources succeeded, but the pod ended up Failed.

The test now waits for plugin2's NodeUnprepareResources call to be recorded before it restarts the kubelet. The restart always interrupts the call the test is named after. After the restart it requires a later NodeUnprepareResources call to succeed, instead of accepting the blocked pre-restart call once the block is lifted. Both new polls take the test context.

`NodeUnprepareResourcesInProgress` matches a call that has been received and has not returned. `NodeUnprepareResourcesSucceededAfter(n)` matches a successful call recorded after the first n calls. Both have unit tests.

The second commit registers the unblock with `DeferCleanup` too, wrapped in `sync.OnceFunc`. Before, a failure earlier in the test left plugin2 blocked through cleanup.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Related to #142404.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
The barrier relies on the test driver recording a call before its handler runs: `recordGRPCCall` appends the entry, calls the handler, then writes the result back at the same index. A blocked call shows up with a nil response.

I could not run the node e2e suite locally against CRI-O. Evidence is the kubelet.log and crio.log of the four failing runs (2101223445017661440, 2101857630149414912, 2102673018894422016, 2103308210961125376) and the crio.log of three passing runs (2103398808246292480, 2103217612228923392, 2102763868420837376). `go vet`, both golangci configs and the matcher unit tests pass.

I reported the two-minute sandbox stop as [cri-o/cri-o#10375](https://github.com/cri-o/cri-o/issues/10375). It reproduces with `crictl` alone. The DRA code plays no part in it.

title: kubelet: honor serverCertificateKeyAlgorithm for the self-signed serving cert
author: antcybersec
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`InitializeTLS` generates a self-signed serving certificate when neither `serverTLSBootstrap` nor an explicit certificate is configured. That path called `GenerateSelfSignedCertKey`, which always produces a 2048-bit RSA key, and ignored `serverCertificateKeyAlgorithm` even though it has `KubeletConfiguration` in hand.

Nothing rejects the combination, so the field is silently dropped: config validation accepts `serverCertificateKeyAlgorithm` regardless of `serverTLSBootstrap`, and only requires TLS 1.3 for the ML-DSA variants. The bootstrapped path already honors the field (`pkg/kubelet/certificate/kubelet.go`), so the two ways a kubelet can get a serving certificate disagreed—and they disagreed even with the field unset, since it documents and defaults to ECDSA-P256 while this path produced RSA-2048.

This PR passes the same key generator the bootstrapped path uses, via the `GenerateKey` option added in #142350. A cluster asking for ML-DSA serving keys now gets them on both paths.

Part of #141838.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

New table test `TestInitializeTLSSelfSignedKeyAlgorithm` asserts the exact key in the generated certificate (curve for ECDSA, bit length for RSA, parameter set for ML-DSA) across unset / ECDSA-P384 / RSA-4096 / ML-DSA-65. Verified all four fail without the change—the unset case reports generated cert key = RSA 2048, want ECDSA P-256.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Kubelet now honors serverCertificateKeyAlgorithm when generating its self-signed serving certificate. Previously that certificate was always RSA-2048; it now uses the configured algorithm, defaulting to ECDSA-P256 as documented.
```

title: Check the new template in ReplicationController update warnings
author: thc1006
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig apps

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`rcStrategy.WarningsOnUpdate` passes the templates in the wrong order:

```go
		warnings = pod.GetWarningsForPodTemplate(ctx, field.NewPath("spec", "template"), oldRc.Spec.Template, newRc.Spec.Template)
```

`GetWarningsForPodTemplate` takes `(ctx, fieldPath, podTemplate, oldPodTemplate)`, and the other workload strategies pass the new template first. So the warnings on a ReplicationController update describe the template it had before the update.

Before and after on a kind cluster. The `###` lines come from my script, which also prints commands without their shell quoting. Its exit-code lines and blank lines are removed and the file path is shortened, the rest is as printed:

```
$ kubectl -n rctest apply -f rc.json
replicationcontroller/rc created
$ kubectl -n rctest patch replicationcontroller rc -p {"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"terminationGracePeriodSeconds":-1}}}}
replicationcontroller/rc patched
$ kubectl -n rctest patch replicationcontroller rc -p {"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"terminationGracePeriodSeconds":30}}}}
Warning: spec.template.spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds: must be >= 0; negative values are invalid and will be treated as 1
replicationcontroller/rc patched
### apiserver v1.38.0-alpha.0.1171+00b5ea25a9b98d

replicationcontroller/rc created

Warning: spec.template.spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds: must be >= 0; negative values are invalid and will be treated as 1
replicationcontroller/rc patched
$ kubectl -n rctest patch replicationcontroller rc -p {"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"terminationGracePeriodSeconds":30}}}}
replicationcontroller/rc patched
```

title: DRA test driver: drop grace period 0 from pod-inline example
author: thc1006
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`test/e2e/dra/test-driver/deploy/example/pod-inline.yaml` still has

```yaml

```

With 0, deleting the example pod does not wait for the kubelet, so the pod can be gone from the API before its claim is unprepared. #131513 ran into that with `pod-external.yaml`, where the claim was recreated under the same name; since #131617 the kubelet rejects a claim whose name it still has cached under another UID. #131585 dropped the line from `pod-external.yaml` and moved both examples to `/agnhost pause`, but the line stayed in `pod-inline.yaml`. title: kubelet: create the gRPC probe client with grpc.NewClient
author: dims
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Moves the gRPC probe from the deprecated `grpc.DialContext` with `WithBlock` to `grpc.NewClient`. The client does no I/O until the health check runs, so the one probe timeout still covers connect and RPC. The target uses the `passthrough` resolver, which hands the address to the probe dialer unresolved, as `DialContext` did by default; `NewClient` would otherwise pick the `dns` resolver. Connection errors now surface from the RPC as `Unavailable` and map to the existing "failed to connect" message.

Behavior change: a refused connection fails the probe at once instead of retrying until `timeoutSeconds`, and a server that never answers reports `timeout: health rpc did not complete within <timeout>` instead of `timeout: failed to connect service`. Probe outcomes do not change.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The unreachable-host test, which asserted the old exact timeout text against port 32, is replaced by a connection-refused test on a closed local port that also checks the probe returns well before its 10s timeout. Precedent: #137955 did the same move for cri-client. The second commit fixes a pre-existing flake in two container lifecycle tests (`exit -1` in busybox) that failed this PR's node e2e run; the comment below has the history.

title: test: remove flaky running wait from DRA extended resource cleanup test
author: siddhanthguptaa
body:
#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The DRA extended resource cleanup tests were flaking because they attempted to observe Pods in the `Running` phase, but the Pods complete so quickly (2-second sleep) that they can transition to `Succeeded` before the wait function observes `Running`.

The `WaitForPodRunningInNamespace` call uses `BeRunningNoRetries()`, which treats `PodSucceeded` as a permanent failure with `gomega.StopTrying`. This causes the test to fail when API server delays, race detection, or test environment load delays observation of the `Running` phase.

The test does not need to observe the `Running` phase. It verifies:

1. The extended resource claim is created.
2. The Pod reaches its expected terminal state (`Succeeded` or `Failed`).
3. The extended resource claim is cleaned up.

Removing the `WaitForPodRunningInNamespace` call eliminates the unnecessary timing dependency while preserving the test's purpose: verifying that extended resource claims are properly cleaned up when Pods complete or fail.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

#142040

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The change intentionally removes the intermediate `Running` wait. The cleanup behavior being tested is tied to Pod terminal state, so observing `Running` is not required for the test invariant.

The existing regular ResourceClaim cleanup tests also wait directly for Pod completion without requiring observation of `Running`.

Local validation:

* `gofmt -l test/e2e/dra/dra.go` passed with no output.
* Reviewed the complete diff; only the intended test change is included.
* The full DRA e2e suite was not run locally because it requires the specialized DRA test environment.

title: fix: create copy of spec to prevent data race
author: matteopulcini6
body:
### What type of PR is this?

/kind flake

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`TestExpectationsOnRecreate` flakes in CI with a data race:

- `FakePodControl.CreatePodsWithGenerateName` sets `spec.GenerateName` on the template it is given.
- The ReplicaSet controller passes `&rs.Spec.Template`, where `rs` comes from the informer lister. The fake is therefore writing into the shared informer cache.
- With `KUBE_CACHE_MUTATION_DETECTOR=true`, the default in `hack/make-rules/test.sh`, the detector goroutine periodically reads cached objects with `reflect.DeepEqual`. That read races with the fake's write, which runs in a goroutine started by `slowStartBatch`.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/142505

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Reproduced locally by temporarily lowering the mutation detector period from 1s to 1ms. That change is not part of this PR.

```
go test -race -c -o /tmp/rs.test ./pkg/controller/replicaset/
KUBE_CACHE_MUTATION_DETECTOR=true stress -p 16 /tmp/rs.test -test.run '^TestExpectationsOnRecreate$'
```

- Before the fix: `DATA RACE` within seconds, with the same stack as CI.
- After the fix: about 1300 runs in 2 minutes, 0 failures.

The `pkg/controller`, `replicaset`, `job` and `daemon` unit tests pass with `-race` and the detector enabled.


title: Fix Quantity.Cmp and AsDec to not modify the Quantity
author: jpbetz
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Fix `Quantity.Cmp`, `AsDec`, and `AsFloat64Slow` to be read-only / threadsafe. This is a follow up on @pohly 's #142277, which fixed `String`.

After this fix these are all read-only / threadsafe:

- `Cmp`, `CmpInt64`, `Equal`, `AsDec`, `AsFloat64Slow`, `AsApproximateFloat64`, `AsInt64`, `AsScaledInt64`, `AsScale`, `AsCanonicalBytes`, `IsZero`, `Sign`, `Value`, `MilliValue`, `ScaledValue`, `String` (via @pohly's fix)
- JSON, CBOR, and protobuf marshalers.

NOT fixed are the functions designed to modify the receiver:
- `ToDec`, `RoundUp`, `Set`, `SetMilli`, `SetScaled`, `CacheString`
- `UnmarshalJSON`, `UnmarshalCBOR`, and protobuf `Unmarshal`
- `Add`, `Sub`, `Mul`, `Neg`

Planned follow-ups (not made worse by this PR):
- `Add`, `Sub`, `Mul`, and `Neg` should return a copy. For example call `b := a` and `a.Add(x)` changes `b`. Also, if `b` had a cached string, `b.String()` still returns the old value, while `b.Cmp` followed by `b.Value` return the new one!
- `NewDecimalQuantity` takes a `inf.Dec` and shallow-copies it. This means that a subsequent write to the caller's `inf.Dec` change the Quantity.
- I'm also considering read-only variants of the mutating functions.  For example, a `WithMili` function could return a copy of the quantity with the milli set and a variant of  `Add` could return the result of addition instead of mutating the receiver.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Part of #141166

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

When an int64-backed Quantity was compared against one backed by `inf.Dec`, `Cmp` called `AsDec`, which switched the receiver to `inf.Dec` in place. On shared objects such as informer caches, that is a data race. It also changes what later reads return: `AsInt64` returns false for an `inf.Dec`-backed Quantity, so in CEL, `x.isLessThan(quantity("1.5Gi")) && x.isInteger()` returned false for `x = 1Gi`. And it complicates the Quantity implementation, which has to handle every state the side effect can leave behind. The comments on #142104 show how complicated that gets.

Separately, `AsDec` returned the receiver's own `inf.Dec`, so writes to the result changed the receiver and every copy of it.

The PR is three commits:

1. Tests that called `AsDec` only to switch to `inf.Dec` now call `ToDec`. On master the two make identical changes, so this commit changes no behavior. Without it, those tests would silently stop covering the `inf.Dec` path after commit 2.
2. `AsDec` returns a copy. This also fixes `Cmp` and `AsFloat64Slow`, which call it.
3. A new unexported `readOnlyDec` returns the internal `inf.Dec` without copying. It is used where the result is only read: `Cmp`, `AsFloat64Slow`, and the argument to `Add` and `Sub`. Without it, commit 2 slows `Cmp` of two `inf.Dec` values from 14ns to 103ns, and from 0 to 4 allocations.

title: test/e2e/dra: keep recorded gRPC calls intact across appends and resets
author: thc1006
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig node

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The DRA test driver's stream interceptor can leave the recorded `Err` nil although the handler returned an error. It happens when another recorded call reallocates the call slice while the stream is open.

`recordGRPCStream` takes a pointer to the last element of the call slice and writes the stream's error through it after the handler returns. Every call recorded in between appends to that slice, and once an append reallocates it, the write goes to the old backing array. `NodeWatchResources` is the only stream and is open for as long as the kubelet keeps its watch on device health, so every other call in that time appends behind it. [#130606](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130606) replaced the index the interceptor used before with this pointer.

The unary interceptor still remembers an index. That survives appends but not `ResetGRPCCalls`, which empties the slice. This PR stores the records behind pointers. Both interceptors append one and fill it in under the mutex when the handler returns, and `GetGRPCCalls` keeps handing out copies. A reset during a call now only detaches that record.

The new tests cover a stream that ends after the slice was reallocated, which fails on master with the error missing, and resets during a call. The unary reset cases check an empty history and a call recorded after the reset, so an old completion can neither bring its record back nor overwrite a newer one. A last one pins that a slice from `GetGRPCCalls` does not change when the call completes or the history is reset.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

title: e2e podlogs: stop busy-looping when the pod watch ends permanently
author: thc1006
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind flake

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

#142127 switched CopyPodLogs to a RetryWatcher so a dropped Pods watch reconnects internally instead of reaching the select loop as a closed channel. That covers a recoverable blip.

A RetryWatcher still closes its result channel for good on a non-retriable error, for example a 410 Gone received mid-watch or invalid credentials. The select case reads the channel without checking whether it is still open, and a receive on a closed channel is always ready, so check() runs on every loop iteration and lists pods continuously until the context is canceled.

The #142026 review asked whether the RetryWatcher could terminate like this; the expectation then was that it always retries. It does for recoverable errors, but not for a non-retriable one. The fix checks the channel and drops it once it closes, so the loop falls back to the existing 30s ticker.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Follow-up to #142127.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The merged integration test (TestCopyPodLogsAPIServerTemporarilyDown) drives the recoverable path with --min-request-timeout, where the RetryWatcher keeps reconnecting. A terminal close is hard to produce reliably against a real apiserver, so the new unit test uses a fake client whose pod watch returns a 410 Gone, which is what sends a RetryWatcher down its terminal path. Without the fix it lists pods hundreds of thousands of times a second; with the fix the count stops growing once the watch closes.

```release-note
NONE
```

title: kubelet: fix FileKeyRef optional file, empty value and whitespace parsing
author: imusmanmalik
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig node

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`FileKeyRef` ignores `optional` when the env file does not exist, and reports a key with an empty value as missing, leaving the container in `CreateContainerConfigError` in both cases. Both come from `ParseEnv` returning only `(string, error)`, which leaves the caller using an empty return value as its not-found sentinel and returning on the open error before it checks `optional`.

`ParseEnv` now also returns whether the key was found, and the caller skips the variable when the file is absent and the reference is optional. The `ConfigMapKeyRef` branch in the same function already distinguishes these cases this way, using the `ok` value from the map lookup.

Only a missing file is treated as skippable. Permission errors, `ENOTDIR`, read failures and syntax errors still fail the container, which matches the ConfigMap and Secret paths where only `IsNotFound` is tolerated.

`ParseEnv` now also rejects `KEY= 'val'`. That line used to be read as an empty value, and the code comment said this matched bash, but bash ends the assignment at the whitespace and runs `val` as a command. Whitespace after `=` followed by nothing or by a comment, as in `KEY=   ` or `KEY= # comment`, still assigns an empty value, as it does in bash. Any other content after that whitespace fails with `unexpected content after whitespace following '='`. Like the existing whitespace-before-`=` check, the error fires for any line the parser reads before it finds the requested key.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #142662

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

`ParseEnv` gains a `found` return. It has one production caller and one test in tree, both updated here. The similarly named `ParseEnv` in `staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/set/env` is a different function and is untouched.

Unit tests:

- `TestMakeEnvironmentVariablesWithFileKeyRef` has five new cases. A missing file with `optional` and a key with an empty value fail before this change with `couldn't parse env file` and `environment variable key "EMPTY" not found in file`. A key written as `EMPTY= # comment` must be published as an empty value. A file containing `DATABASE= 'db'`, referenced with `optional` unset and set, must fail in both cases.
- `TestParseEnv` has eight new cases for the text after `=`. The old parser accepts `KEY1= 'val1'` (for that key and for a later one) and `KEY1= val1`, so those cases fail on it with `expected error, got none`. `KEY1=#x` must also fail, as it already did, because bash reads it as the value `#x`. `KEY1=   `, `KEY1= # comment` and a tab followed by a comment must give an empty value, and a later key in the same file must still be found. These empty cases run through the existing `bash --posix` cross-check. A `wantNotFound` field keeps the empty-value and absent-key cases apart.

e2e tests in `test/e2e/common/node/file_key.go`:

- `should handle o

title: podgroupprotection: forget keys on success and requeue on error
author: parthksingh1
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind regression

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`processNextWorkItem` in the PodGroup protection controller has its error check inverted (regressed in #141021 when the function was generalised to serve both the PodGroup and CompositePodGroup queues):

- On success, the key was requeued with `AddRateLimited` forever and logged as `PodGroup <key> failed with: %!w(<nil>)`. This also applies to keys for objects that were already deleted, so the rate limiter's per-item state grows with every PodGroup the controller has seen.
- On error (e.g. a 409 Conflict while removing the finalizer), the key was `Forget`-ed and dropped, so a PodGroup/CompositePodGroup being deleted could stay in `Terminating` until the next informer resync.

This PR restores the `err == nil` check from the original implementation (#137641) and adds `TestProcessNextWorkItem`, which covers both paths. The existing tests call `processPodGroup`/`processCompositePodGroup` directly, which is why the regression was not caught. The new test fails on the current code and passes with the fix.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #142827

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The regression is in v1.38.0-alpha.2 only; no stable release is affected.

title: tests: reduce testing.T/TB usage
author: pohly
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Helper code which requires testing.T or testing.TB is often unnecessarily restrictive, which limits its usefulness. In particular, a ktesting.TContext instance cannot be used even though it typically implements everything that the helper code needs.

The solution depends on the context:
- Using a locally-defined interface avoids adding dependencies.
- The new test/utils.TB is a minimal reusable interface for those cases where a local interface would be too repetitive.
- In some cases, ktesting.TB is required.

Unnecessary usage of testing.T/TB can be prevented with forbidigo. This revealed some interesting and broken usage like passing `&testing.T{}` as parameter: such an empty struct works for Log calls, but Fatal and FailNow crash ("test executed panic(nil) or runtime.Goexit"). In E2E tests, GinkgoTB() can be used instead. Elsewhere, the new FatalToError captures failures and adds them to the caller's error return value.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137133 has to use a mixture of tCtx and t because helper code unnecessarily requires testing.T.

title: e2e: retry CockroachDB reads instead of failing on the first exec error
author: dims
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind flake

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Found when digging into ci failures in:
https://testgrid.k8s.io/amazon-ec2-release#ec2-master-scale-correctness-100

`[sig-apps] StatefulSet Deploy clustered applications should creating a working CockroachDB cluster [Slow]` fails intermittently right after the StatefulSet restart. The first `cockroach sql` exec on the recreated pod hits either `lookup cockroachdb-2.cockroachdb on <kube-dns>:53: no such host` (CoreDNS still serves a cached negative answer for the pod's headless Service record; with `ttl 30` in the kubernetes plugin that is also the SOA minimum TTL for NXDOMAIN) or `dial tcp <pod-ip>:26257: connect: connection refused` (the node is not serving SQL yet).

`read()` used `RunKubectlOrDie`, so that first error ended the spec and the 60s `pollReadWithTimeout` loop never got to retry. This returns an empty value on exec errors so the existing poll retries. `cockroachDBExec` now returns the error; `deploy` and `write` keep failing hard through `framework.ExpectNoError`.

Seen in 8 of the last 29 runs of `ci-kubernetes-e2e-ec2-scale-correctness-100` (the read happened 0.6s to 9.9s after the recreated pod's container started) and in the kops gce/aws slow canaries.

title: Job: do not decrement Ready when pod delete fails
author: yankovitchg
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When the Job controller deletes pods, it also adjusts `status.ready` by counting how many of those pods were Ready. Two helpers did that incorrectly when `DeletePod` failed:

- `deleteActivePods` (Job failed / finished: delete remaining active pods) always counted a Ready pod toward `deletedReady`, even if the delete errored.
- `deleteJobPods` (scale-down when over parallelism, suspend, etc.: patch tracking finalizer then delete) did the same after a failed `DeletePod`.

Callers then subtract that count from `jobCtx.ready`, so a failed delete could undercount Ready until a later sync corrected it.

This PR only decrements Ready when the delete actually succeeded (or the pod was already gone / `NotFound`).

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- `deleteActivePods`: Ready increment moved into the success branch (`else if`).
- `deleteJobPods`: Ready increment gated on `err == nil || apierrors.IsNotFound(err)` (same success notion as the delete path).
- Tests: `FakePodControl.DeleteErr` so Patch can succeed while Delete fails (needed for `deleteJobPods`). New `TestControllerSyncJob` cases for scale-down and job-fail paths.

/sig apps

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Job status.ready no longer decreases when deleting a Ready pod fails.
```

title: Fix job_pods_creation_total double-counting failed creates

body:
